title: Court raps FSL Rohini for delaying report in four-year-old riots case
Text: Pulling up the Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) at Rohini for a delayed report in a four-year-old Northeast Delhi riots case, a city court Monday directed the director to appear before it in person on August 7 to provide a justification for being non- responsive to letters sent by the court. The court was hearing a case related to the 2020 riots, in which construction workers at a school near TB Hospital, Karawal Nagar, were killed by a mob. Charges were framed against four accused in this case in December 2021 by Additional Sessions Judge Virender Bhat. “In these circumstances, issue court notice to ld. Director, FSL, Rohini, to appear in person to offer any justification for being non-responsive to the letters of request as sent in this case, as well as in several other cases, by this court,” said Additional Sessions Judge Pulastya Pramachala.

title: Leaders of all 10 tribal councils in Northeast unite to push demands, meet Shah in Delhi
Text: A joint forum of the Chief Executive Members (CEMs) of all 10 Autonomous District Councils (ADCs) from the Northeast met Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Thursday to push for the passing of a Bill that would amend the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution and increase these councils’ powers and funds. The 10 ADCs under the Sixth Schedule comprise three each from Assam, Meghalaya and Mizoram, and one from Tripura. These are elected bodies that have jurisdiction – with limited executive, legislative and financial powers – over specific tribal-majority areas. Their objective is to ensure development in these areas and boost self-government by tribal communities. Text: After having won the Jalandhar (West) Assembly elections, the AAP has already got into election mode for four more assembly by-elections, even as the Election Commission of India is yet to announce the bypolls. title: In maiden Budget, Odisha’s BJP govt sheds ‘Biju’ stamp, gives old schemes a new twist
Text: Old schemes with new branding. That appeared to be a recurrent theme as Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi’s maiden Budget was presented in the state assembly on Thursday. The state’s total Budget outlay was Rs 2.65 lakh crore — 15 percent more than the last Budget under the previous Biju Janata Dal (BJD) government. Under SUBHADRA, planned to launch on September 17 — Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday — the government has plans to give vouchers of up to Rs 50,000 to women, which can be encashed in two years. Text: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit the Kargil War Memorial on Friday and pay homage to the bravehearts who made the supreme sacrifice in the line of duty, his office said on Thursday. “On the occasion of the 25th Kargil Vijay Diwas on 26th July 2024, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will visit the Kargil War Memorial and pay homage to the bravehearts who made the supreme sacrifice in the line of duty,” the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said in a statement. The PM will also virtually carry out the first blast of the Shinkun La Tunnel Project, which consists of a 4.1-km-long twin-tube tunnel which will be constructed at an altitude of around 15,800 feet on the Nimu-Padum-Darcha road to provide all-weather connectivity to Leh, it said. Once completed, it will be the highest tunnel in the world.

Text: Power bills are all set to go up in Chandigarh from August 1 as the Joint Electricity Regulatory Commission (JERC) approved a hike of 9.40 per cent power tariff. Although the tariff is much less than the proposed hike of 19 per cent as proposed by Chandigarh Administration, the bills shall rise by 9.40 per cent. title: How pet dogs saved 2 sisters from attack by Ghaziabad neighbours
Text: Late on Tuesday, two sisters, residents of Khoda in Ghaziabad, received a knock on their door. On the other side was a group of neighbours they had an argument with a few minutes back over walking their pet dogs on the lane outside. As they opened their gate, an argument ensued between the two sides and soon, one of the men took out a knife to attack the sisters, both in their 20s. At this, two of their three pet dogs jumped in, attacked the men and sent them packing from the house. title: Disappointed with timing, symbolism of Modi’s visit to Russia: US
Text: The United States is disappointed about the symbolism and timing of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Russia visit at a time when it hosted the NATO summit here, a senior State Department official has told the lawmakers, who have expressed concerns over the increasing India-Russia ties. “I could not agree with you more about our disappointment about the symbolism and the timing of Prime Minister Modi’s trip to Moscow. We are having those tough conversations with our Indian friends,” Assistant Secretary of State for South and Central Asia Donald Lu told American lawmakers at a Congressional hearing here on Tuesday. “I assure you, may be if I could just take a moment to put into context that visit. title: Took Centre 5 decades to realise ‘mistake’ of placing RSS in ‘ban list’: Madhya Pradesh High Court, which heard retd govt official’s petition
Text: It took five decades for the central government to realise its “mistake” of wrongly placing “an internationally renowned organisation like Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh” in the list of organisations government officials cannot be associated with, the Madhya Pradesh High Court observed on Thursday. The court was hearing a petition filed by Indore resident Purushottam Gupta, a retired central government officer, who had in September 2023 knocked on the court’s doors, saying rules that barred him from joining the RSS were “an impediment for him to gratify his desires at the dusk of his life”. title: 1 person holds 32 faculty posts, 211 filled 2,500 vacancies: Anna University rocked by ‘phantom’ professors in colleges
Text: After a Chennai-based anti-corruption group, Arappor Iyakkam, found that a large number of faculty positions in engineering colleges affiliated to Anna University were filled by “phantom” professors, the university, in its own investigation, found that 211 people filled around 2,500 vacancies across multiple colleges, with instances of a single person holding over 30 different posts. Anna University Vice Chancellor R Velraj told The Indian Express that his office found these 211 people were working as full-time faculty in multiple colleges. “This doesn’t mean that they were working in all colleges at the same time. It is just on the records. Colleges have done it to retain their affiliation during the inspections done by the university. Text: Several investors have accused the operator of World Trade Centre (Noida) Development Company, builder Ashish Bhalla, of embezzling billions of rupees. title: Delhi-NCR wake up to heavy rain; IMD issues yellow alert and predicts more showers today
Text: As heavy rain lashed many parts of Delhi and the National Capital Region (NCR) on Friday morning, several areas in the national capital witnessed waterlogged streets and traffic snarls. The India Meteorological Department (IMD), which has issued a yellow alert (be aware) in the Capital till Sunday, predicted moderate rain and a generally cloudy sky on Friday as per its seven-day forecast. The yellow alert has been issued in all regions of Delhi-NCR, except for Northwest NCR, in the IMD’s Nowcast valid till 10.15 am. Text: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann on Thursday announced that the state government would boycott the NITI Aayog meeting to be chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on July 27. Interacting with mediapersons during his two-day visit to Jalandhar to listen to the grievances of the people from the Doaba and Majha regions at his Jalandhar residence, the chief minister said the decision was taken after the Union Budget failed to allocate funds to Punjab despite the state’s significant contributions to the nation. Mann termed the Union Budget a ‘Kursi Bachao Budget’ (Save the Chair Budget), accusing the Centre of political vendetta against non-BJP ruled states.

title: Doctor tests positive of swine flu in Chandigarh
Text: A day after the Health Department, Chandigarh issued an advisory for seasonal influenza, a H1N1, Chandigarh reported a case of swine flu, with a doctor in a local hospital testing positive. The condition of the patient is said to be stable. The doctor is being treated at GMSH-16, Chandigarh and is kept under observation. The family\close contacts of the doctor are also being monitored for any symptoms. H1N1 flu is also known as swine flu and spreads in the same manner as the seasonal flu. When people who have the flu, cough or sneeze, drops of virus are sprayed in the air, and that’s how the flu spreads. While influenza is a seasonal occurrence, in monsoons due to increased humidity the environment is conducive for the circulation of a number of viral respiratory pathogens like Influenza A (H1N1), adenoviruses etc.

title: Gujarat confidential: Bonhomie
Text: Imam Umer Ahmed Ilyasi, chief Imam of All India Imam Organisation, recently met Dabhoi BJP MLA Shailesh Mehta at his residence in Vadodara. BSV, based in Mumbai, was originally promoted by the Daftary family. Advertisement Advent acquired a 74 per cent stake in BSV in February 2020, providing a complete exit to private equity investors OrbiMed Asia and Kotak PE and a partial exit to the promoter Daftary family. Advent bought the remaining 26 per cent stake from the Daftary family later following approval from the Department of Pharmaceuticals.

title: ‘Extortion racket’ busted in UP, 18 cops suspended
Text: EIGHTEEN POLICEMEN, including the station officer (SO) of a police station in Ballia district were suspended and 16 persons, including two policemen, were arrested on charges of extortion and corruption, officers said on Thursday. The action was taken after the Additional Director General (Varanasi Zone) and Deputy Inspector General (Azamgarh Range) unearthed an “extortion racket” in an operation conducted late evening on Wednesday and nabbed the cops and 16 others red-handed, the officers added. On the basis of a report submitted to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Thursday evening, the Ballia Superintendent of Police and Additional Superintendent of Police of Ballia have been transferred and put on waiting, while the local Circle Officer (Deputy SP) has been suspended.

title: Speaker Birla warns of action if members speak against Chair
Text: LOK SABHA Speaker Om Birla on Thursday warned of action against members who would on record speak against the Chair in the House. He also advised the MPs “not to say anything about the Chair even when the proceedings are not being recorded”. “Even when unrecorded, members say things, even about the Chair. If you speak against the Chair on record, I will take action… Members of all parties sit in the Chair and do so with dignity,” the Speaker said just after 2 pm. Advertisement The Speaker also urged the members on both sides “not to cross the line” during the debates. “No member of any party, and also ministers… let us not lower the dignity of the House…,” Birla said. He made the reference to ministers when Congress leader K C Venugopal said a minister walked towards the Opposition benches, which he saw as an attempt to “attack” them. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh intervened and said anything deemed unparliamentary or below the dignity of the House should be expunged so that the House can run peacefully.

title: End of Old Tax Regime would depend on the acceptability of new regime among taxpayers: CBDT Chairman Ravi Agrawal
Text: The government further sweetened the New Tax Regime in the Union Budget for 2024-25, hoping that the move will nudge more salaried taxpayers to migrate to the relatively simple and exemption-free income tax format. According to RAVI AGRAWAL, Chairman of the Central Board of Direct Taxes, taxpayers were already switching to the NTR in large numbers, and the latest rejig is expected to accelerate the process further. Does that mean that the end of the road for the Old Tax Regime is on the horizon? Agarwal says that it will depend on how the acceptability of the NTR grows. In an Interaction with AGGAM WALIA and SUKALP SHARMA, Agarwal delves into the NTR and other key direct tax-related moves in the Budget, including the changes in capital gains tax, scrapping of the so-called Angel Tax, and the planned comprehensive review of the Income Tax Act. Edited excerpts: Advertisement While the New Tax Regime has been made more attractive, there is a feeling in some sections that the additional tax savings are not substantial. This is all a relative concept. The counter question would be: What would be an adequate amount? Rs 20,000, Rs 25,000, or Rs 30,000, or Rs 40,000?

title: Top 500 firms likely to get ‘quota’ for interns based on CSR spend
Text: THE GOVERNMENT plans to talk to the top 500 companies and mutually agree on a “voluntary quota system” for taking on board interns under the employment package announced in the Budget 2024-25. The “quota system” would be based on the Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) expenditure of these companies, Finance Secretary TV Somanathan told The Indian Express. “Details are yet to be worked out, and will be done in consultation with the industry. We might perhaps have some kind of voluntary quota system, mutually agreed upon, saying that you will take so much or this much based on your CSR expenditure. We will also permit them to use their backward and forward supply chain for skilling,” Somanathan said. Advertisement The government is keen to ensure that those at the margins are able to make the most of this internship scheme. “We won’t be giving them (companies) the type of people they would normally recruit because we don’t want to give them a subsidy for people they would have hired anyway. We will have a negative list also: Say, nobody from IITs, IIMs, chartered accountants, cost accountants, nobody who is paying income tax, nobody whose parent is a government servant, etc. We

title: Toddler dead, 2 missing in Surat as Mithi creek floods
Text: A two-year-old boy died and two youths are feared dead in Surat, as the Mithi creek flooded on Thursday. The bodies of the youths are yet to be recovered. According to the Surat Municipal Commission (SMC), the toddler, Altaf Khan, died at Kamrunagar in Limbayat, which is under water due to flooding of Mithi creek. Surat fire officer Kirti Modh said, “We were in a boat, distributing food packets at Kamrunagar… we came to know that Altaf, who was in the arms of his mother Sumaiya Khan, had accidentally fallen into the water from the second floor of their building.”

title: TRP Game zone fire: Statements of 37 witnesses, partnership deed among key evidence in chargeseet
Text: To make its case stronger in the TRP Game Zone fire case, the special investigation team (SIT) of the Rajkot City Police has appended the statements of 37 witnesses recorded by the magistrate to the chargesheet – running into over a lakh pages – it filed against 15 accused in a court on Wednesday. Parthrajsinh Gohil, Rajkot Deputy Commissioner of Police (Crime), who was supervising the SIT investigation, told The Indian Express: “We have done a thorough investigation and left no stone unturned to unearth the truth and build a watertight case against the accused.” Advertisement “To ensure that the case holds during the trial, even if witnesses turn hostile, we have got statements of 37 key witnesses recorded by the magistrate under CrPC (Criminal Procedure Code) Section 164 and appended them to the chargesheet,” he added.

title: 2008 Malegaon blast was planned to terrorise people: NIA begins final arguments
Text: THE NATIONAL Investigation Agency (NIA) began its final arguments in the Malegaon 2008 blast case, claiming that the blast was planned with an intention to terrorise people and create communal rift. Special public prosecutors Avinash Rasal and Anushree Rasal submitted that on September 29, 2008, a bomb explosion took place at Malegaon in the month of Ramzan, with the bomb fitted on a LML Freedom Motorcycle. Six persons were killed and over 100 injured. “The bomb blast was caused by the conspirators with the intent to terrorise people, to cause loss of life and property. The explosion was carried out with an intention to disrupt supplies and services essential to a community, to create communal rift and to endanger internal security of the state,” the prosecutors told the court.

title: Take no fee from girl students at time of admission: Chandrakant Patil
Text: Days after announcing that the state government will extend 100 per cent reimbursement of tuition and examination fees for girls pursuing professional courses who come from families having an annual income of Rs.8 lakh, higher and technical education minister Chandrakant Patil on Thursday clarified that colleges are instructed not to take fees from girls at the time of admissions and that the government will pay the fees in two installments. “Colleges have been given clear instructions that no girl should have to pay the fees at the time of admission and that the fee will be reimbursed by the government later. If any college asks students to pay fees upfront at the time of admission, it should be reported to the higher and technical education department,” said Patil as he was interacting with students and other stakeholders in a webinar on Thursday aiming to clarify doubts around the recently announced scheme. He said that the rate of enrolment of girls in professional courses is only 34 percent in Maharashtra as opposed to 64 per cent in case of boys.

title: Maharashtra state board exams rescheduled due to heavy rain warning
Text: Due to warning of heavy rain, Maharashtra State Board of Secondary and Higher Secondary Education (MSBSHSE) has rescheduled papers to be held on Friday, in an ongoing repeaters examination for Secondary School Certificate (SSC) and Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC). As per a notification issued by the Maharashtra State Board, for SSC exams, paper of Science and Technology part 2 was scheduled to be held on July 26 in the morning session from 11 am to 1pm. It will now be held on July 31 in the morning session. Whereas for HSC, exams three papers were scheduled to be held on Friday – Commerce and Management, Food Technology and MCVC paper 2, in morning session – from 11am to 1pm. All these papers will now be held on August 9 in the same session.

title: Bangladesh objected to Mamata’s ‘shelter’ remarks, says MEA
Text: India has received a diplomatic note from the Bangladesh government, objecting to West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee’s remarks about giving shelter to Bangladeshi citizens fleeing the country in the wake of violent protests, the Ministry of External Affairs said Thursday. It also said that all matters pertaining to foreign affairs are the sole prerogative of the Cente, when asked about Banerjee’s comments and recent reports on Kerala ‘appointing’ one of its bureaucrats as ‘foreign secretary’. “I can confirm that we have received such a communication from the Bangladesh side. It is on the lines described in the reports,” said MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal on Thursday.

title: Shirur landslide: Rescuers close in on Arjun’s truck
Text: The drone team headed by Rtd Maj Gen M Indrabalan Thursday confirmed that Kerala based Arjun’s truck is likely to be in the downstream area of the Gangavali river. This was achieved using the Ebinger Ferromagnetic Locator which is a Drone Intelligent Buried Object Detection System (DIBODS) deployed for the operations to locate the missing cabin of Arjun’s truck in the landslide hit region of Shirur. Advertisement Indrabalan, after the drone operation said that there is a possibility of the truck not being disintegrated into pieces because of its monolithic design. (Express photo) Indrabalan, after the drone operation said that there is a possibility of the truck not being disintegrated into pieces because of its monolithic design. (Express photo) This comes a day after the rescuers locked the coordinates of the truck using ISRO’s satellite images. The locator provided by CME Pune identified four distinct spots – widely separated – out of which two spots (in the downstream) indicated the possibility of truck container and the cabin, another spot indicating the road railings beneath the river. The operators are yet to ascertain the contents in the fourth spot.

title: Madan Rathore replaces C P Joshi as Rajasthan BJP president
Text: The BJP Thursday announced Rajya Sabha MP Madan Rathore as party’s Rajasthan state president, replacing Lok Sabha MP C P Joshi. The party also announced its Rajya Sabha MP Dr Radha Mohan Das Agrawal as party in charge of Rajasthan with party national secretary Vijaya Rahatkar as co-in-charge of the state BJP. Madan Rathore, 69, is a native of Pali district and was MLA twice during Vasundhara Raje’s two tenures as Chief Minister between 2003-08 and 2013-18. He started out as a Pracharak with the RSS in Pali in the 1970s, before moving on to the BJP in the mid-1980s. After holding various posts in the Pali district unit of the BJP, he moved to the state unit. He won from Sumerpur Assembly in Pali district twice, defeating Congress leader Bina Kak both times. Between 2014 and 2018, he was the BJP Deputy Chief Whip in the state Assembly.

title: IIT-Kgp bestows Pichai with Doctor of Science, wife Anjali Distinguished Alumnus Award in San Francisco
Text: IIT-Kharagpur honoured Google CEO Sundar Pichai with the Doctor of Science (Honoris Causa) Award and his wife Anjali Pichai with Distinguished Alumnus Award at a programme in San Francisco in the US, said a statement issued by the institute on Thursday. The felicitation was done in the presence of VK Tewari, Director, IIT-Kharagpur, and Sundar Pichai’s parents and their daughter Kavya Pichai. Advertisement “In recognition of his remarkable contribution towards digital transformation, affordable technology and pathbreaking innovations; President Droupadi Murmu, Visitor of the institute, bestowed the degree of Doctor of Science (Honoris Causa) to Pichai in absentia at the 69th Convocation of IIT-Kharagpur in December last year. However, as Pichai was not present at the annual convocation, the institute therefore had decided to reach out to him at a later date for the same. On July 23, the institute officials held the felicitation programme in San Francisco,” the institute said.

title: Jaishankar tells Chinese counterpart to ‘ensure full respect for LAC’ during ASEAN meet
Text: In a meeting with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar emphasised on the need to respect the past agreements and ensure “full respect” for the Line of Actual Control (LAC). The two foreign ministers met at the sidelines of the ASEAN Summit in Vientiane. Jaishankar met Yi for the second time in the month of July and discussed resolving the issues at LAC. It gave an opportunity to both the leaders to review the work done since they last met on the margins of Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit in Astana on July 4. Met with CPC Politburo member and FM Wang Yi in Vientiane today. Continued our ongoing discussions about our bilateral relationship. title: Chandigarh administration cancels Berkeley and Godrej’s occupation certificates
Text: The Chandigarh Administration on Thursday ordered the cancellation of occupation certificate and building plans of two prominent buildings of the city. Both Berkeley Square and Godrej buildings in the Industrial Area phase I have said to have violated environmental norms. Both the buildings have over 100 key businesses running from their complexes. Confirming the development, Chandigarh Deputy Commissioner Vinay Pratap Singh told The Indian Express, “Yes. Orders have been issued for violations of conditions of environmental clearance regarding obtaining permission from the Standing Committee of National Board for Wildlife. Based on such environmental clearance whose major condition regarding wildlife clearance is still unfulfilled, building plans and occupation certificates of these buildings were issued. Hence both building plans and occupation certificates have been revoked.” Advertisement Not only this, but the DC has also directed the enforcement branch to ensure compliance with the order and put up a compliance report for record within a week. The enforcement agencies have been asked to ensure that the building is not put to habitable use any further after revocation of occupation certificate. After the State Environment Impact Assessment Authority (SEIAA), Chandigarh, had stated that both the buildings had misrepresented the issue of wildlife clearance and

title: Congress worker ‘beaten to death’ in Jalpaiguri, 5 held
Text: A Congress worker was beaten to death in Jalpaiguri on Wednesday night, said police, adding five persons have been arrested in connection with the incident. According to police, a group of people tied 48-year-old Manik Roy to a tree and beat him with rods and sticks on Wednesday night near his house at Hathat colony under Khargrabari-1 gram panchayat of Maynaguri in Jalpaiguri district. After Roy’s family alerted the police, he was rescued and brought to Jalpaiguri General Hospital where he succumbed to his injuries later. Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. According to the Congress, Roy, an active worker of the party was forced to leave his house after the Lok Sabha polls as he started getting threats from TMC-backed goons.

title: India’s stern reply to US on PM Modi’s Russia visit, says ‘Have freedom of choice in foreign relations’
Text: India, in a stern reply to US regarding PM Narendra Modi’s visit to Russia earlier this month, said that all countries have a “freedom of choice” in a multipolar world regarding foreign relations. External Affairs Ministry Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal was asked about the comment by a US official and he said that India has had a long relationship with Russia which is based upon the “mutual interest”. The Ministry of External Affairs on July 25 reacted sharply to a comment by US Assistant Secretary of State for South and Central Asia, Donald Lu, on PM Modi visiting Moscow. Regarding the comments made by American diplomat Donald Lu about India, @MEAIndia Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal says, “You must understand that India has a long-standing relationship with Russia that is based on mutual interests in a multipolar world. All countries have the… pic.twitter.com/oJKYWnIMbw — All India Radio News (@airnewsalerts) July 25, 2024 Lu told the US Congress on Tuesday that America was disappointed by “symbolism and timing” of PM Modi’s visit to Russia. Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. Lu told the US lawmakers that “I could not agree with you more about our disappointment about the symbolism and the timing

title: Bangalore Development Authority incurred Rs 3,500 cr ‘loss’ by not collecting betterment tax: CAG
Text: The “lackadaisical effort” of the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) in raising internal revenue from legally enforceable avenues indicated “poor financial management”, the Comptroller and Auditor General has said, while pointing to Rs 3,500 crore “loss” by not collecting betterment tax. The CAG’s compliance audit report on Department and Public Sector Undertakings for the year ended March 2022, was tabled in the Assembly on Thursday. The audit observed that as against the projected betterment tax of Rs 3,307.55 crore from Arkavathy layout and Rs 195.72 crore from Nada Prabhu Kempegowda Layout (NPKL), the BDA could collect only Rs 3.22 crore from April 2019 to March 2022. Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. BDA did not make efforts for collection of betterment tax as the procedures prescribed under the Act were not followed, it said.

title: PM Modi to visit Kargil on Friday on 25th Kargil Vijay Diwas
Text: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit the Kargil War Memorial on July 26 and pay homage to the bravehearts who made the supreme sacrifice in the line of duty, his office said on Thursday. The prime minister will also carry out the first blast of the Shinkun La Tunnel Project virtually. “On the occasion of the 25th Kargil Vijay Diwas on 26th July 2024, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will visit the Kargil War Memorial at around 9:20 AM and pay homage to the bravehearts who made the supreme sacrifice in the line of duty,” the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said in a statement.

title: Day 2 of Budget discussion: In LS, Opp calls Budget ‘most divisive’, BJP touts fiscal management
Text: For the second day running, the discussion on the Budget turned into a war of words as the Opposition termed it “divisive” and raised the issues of jobs and farmers. The BJP, meanwhile, called the Budget “historic” and praised the government’s fiscal management. Former Punjab chief minister and Congress member Charanjit Singh Channi said the Budget was aimed at saving the government rather than the country. “Farmers are called Khalistani when they make demands, which aren’t fulfilled. This is also an emergency,” he said. Channi asked why there cannot be a legal guarantee for MSP, adding that 736 people had been killed during the farm protests. Union Minister Piyush Goyal accused Channi of misguiding the people and said he had to authenticate whatever he said on the floor of the House, demanding action if he did not. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said that there was nothing wrong in a minister demanding authentication, and that this should be seen as a matter of privilege. During the discussion, TMC member Saugata Roy said Nirmala Sitharaman is not a “trained economist”. “I do not expect the Finance Minister (Nirmala Sitharaman) to be like Dr Manmohan Singh, she is not a PhD from

title: Citing Arvind Kejriwal’s bail order, court in Mumbai frees PMLA accused
Text: Citing the Supreme Court order granting bail to Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal, a special court in Mumbai granted bail to an accused in a money laundering case on the grounds that the Enforcement Directorate did not supply him the “reasons to believe” that he could be arrested. “On bare perusal of judgment in the matter of Arvind Kejriwal, it becomes mandate to provide the reasons to believe invoking Section 19 of PMLA, 2002 to the accused,” the order stated, while directing the release of the accused since his remand itself is not tenable. The ED had arrested Purushottam Mandhana on April 19, linked to Rs 975 crore alleged bank loan fraud case. Mandhana was sent to ED’s custody till Thursday. On being produced before the court on Thursday, Mandhana, through his lawyers, told the court that the Supreme Court in a recent ruling while granting interim bail to Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal in the ED case, had referred to a benchmark for arrest under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). The ED officer is required to record his reasons to believe that the accused is guilty of the offence. A copy of this is also required to

title: Chandipura virus: 4-member team continues survey in Panchmahal
Text: A four-member team of experts from Pune’s National Institute of Virology (NIV) continued its survey in Panchmahal, which has recorded five deaths suspected due to Chandipura virus, for the third day Thursday, even as the total number of suspected cases has increased to 118 in the state. The team — comprising two scientists and two technical staff — has visited the residence of the five children from the district who succumbed to the virus in the beginning of July. The experts visited the homes of a four-year-old in Kotda village, an eight-year-old from Ghoghambha and a one-and-half-year old from Khanpur village, among others, and collected samples of their family members, neighbours as well as cattle owned by them. The experts also gathered the samples of sandflies during their visit.

title: Three arrested for theft of antique items in Surat
Text: Three persons were arrested on Wednesday night for allegedly stealing antique items from farmhouses and weekend homes at Dumas in Surat. The police identified the three men as Shaukat alias Shanker Rathod (43) and Sunil Rathod (21) from Althan and Tejas Rathod (30) from Umra village. Antique items likes vessels and idols made of copper as well as jewellery were recovered from them, the police added. Dumas police Inspector N V Bharwad said, “Our teams were patrolling the silent zone area near Surat International Airport, when Shaukat and Sunil were spotted carrying suspicious in their bags. They were stopped and when searched, two copper idols were recovered.”

title: Opp attacks govt on taxes, unemployment and farm incomes in Rajya Sabha
Text: Opposition parties Thursday continued their attack on the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) government in Rajya Sabha, criticising the Budget on issues of taxes, farm incomes and unemployment. On the second day of the Budget discussion, the Opposition’s charge was led by Congress’ Randeep Surjewala, Aam Aadmi Party’s (AAP) Raghav Chadha and independent member Kapil Sibal. Opposition MP’s also criticised the Budget for ignoring the aspirations of other states while favouring Bihar and Andhra Pradesh with a slew of project announcements. Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MP’s Medha Kulkarni and former Minister of State Bhagwat Karad countered the Opposition’s criticism, listing out the government’s allocation to other states and highlighting schemes targeted for farmer and youth welfare. Advertisement Randeep Surjwala, who was the first to speak during the Budget discussion on Thursday, charged the government with failure to fulfil their promise of doubling the income of farmers. “When the Finance Minister began the Budget speech with three words; farmers poor and youth, the whole nation was filled with expectations but within a few minutes it was clear this budget is “kursi bachao, sahiyogi dal patao, aur haar la badla lete jao budget (save the government, placate the allies and extract revenge for

title: No pollution control permits for ‘white category’ sectors now
Text: Those industries which are practically non-polluting and categorised under the ‘white category’ by the Central Pollution Control Board will now not require prior permission of the state pollution control boards to establish and operate under the Air Act, 1981 and Water Act, 1974, according to two separate draft notifications of the Environment Ministry. These permissions known officially as ‘consent to establish’ (CTE) and ‘consent to operate’ (CTO) are granted to regulate industries that discharge effluents or emit pollutants into the environment. The ministry has also proposed to do away with the CTE permit for “projects/activities” that require prior environmental clearance (EC).

title: Govt launches revamped scheme to facilitate skill loans of up to Rs 7.5L
Text: A revamped ‘model skill loan scheme’ for skill development courses was launched by the government on Thursday, with a fresh maximum loan limit of Rs 7.5 lakh — up from the previous amount of Rs 1.5 lakh. In her budget speech on Tuesday, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman had announced that the model skill loan scheme will be “revised to facilitate loans up to Rs 7.5 lakh, with a guarantee from a government-promoted fund”. “This is expected to help 25,000 students every year,” Sitharaman had said. Launched in 2015, the reversion of the old scheme had been recording a low uptake. Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. Going by data presented at the launch of the revised scheme on Thursday, loans amounting to Rs 115.75 crore were extended to 10,077 borrowers until March 31 this year. The low fund utilisation has been attributed to the maximum loan limit of Rs 1.5 lakh and increase in fees for courses, leading to high-cost courses being out of the old scheme. Now, the revised scheme will see a broadened lending framework.

title: India demands strong, swift action against temple vandals in Canada
Text: Following reports of “vandalisation of a Hindu temple” in Canada’s Edmonton, New Delhi has registered a strong protest with Ottawa and demanded prompt action against those behind the attack. On Monday, the BAPS Swaminarayan Temple in Edmonton was “defaced with anti-India graffiti and slurs”. Condemning the attack, Indian-origin Canadian MP Chandra Arya posted on X: “During the last few years, Hindu temples in the Greater Toronto Area, British Columbia, and other places in Canada being vandalised with hateful graffiti.” Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. Talking to reporters on Thursday, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said: “We have strongly taken up the matter with the Canadian authorities, both in Delhi and Ottawa. We condemn the vandalisation, and expect the local authorities to take strong and swift action against those responsible.”

title: UP police constable re-exam in August: Govt
Text: OVER FOUR months after an alleged paper leak and subsequent cancellation of the polce constable recruitment examination, the Uttar Pradesh government on Thursday announced fresh dates for re-examination. The Uttar Pradesh Police Recruitment and Promotion Board will conduct the written exam to fill 60,244 Civil Police positions on August 23, 24, 25 and August 30, 31, 2024. The exam was earlier cancelled after demand by students over allegations of a paper leak. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath then directed the officials concerned to reschedule the exam within six months, ensuring adherence to the “standards of fairness and transparency.” Detailed guidelines were issued in this regard by the BJP government in the state on June 19, 2024. These guidelines cover all aspects of the examination, including preparation, selection of centres, candidate verification and measures to prevent impersonation. The Board has been asked to conduct the exam strictly adhering to these standards.

title: 57% of pending govt litigation pertains to Finance, Railways, Defence: Data
Text: Over 57% of the 6.98 lakh pending court cases in which the Union government is a litigant pertains to three ministries — Finance, Railways and Defence — according to Law Ministry data given to the Rajya Sabha on Thursday. Replying to a question by BJP MP Neeraj Shekhar on pending cases, Minister of State (independent charge) for Law and Justice Arjun Ram Meghwal said the data on pending government litigation was “dynamic and kept changing”. However, he provided the data from Legal Information Management and Briefing System (LIMBS), on which ministries enter their own case details. As per the LIMBS data on July 19, there were 6,98,904 pending cases in which the government was a litigant. The highest number of pending cases pertained to the Ministry of Finance (1.89 lakh), followed by the Railways (1.14 lakh) and Defence Ministry (95,467). Labour and Employment Ministry had 79,988 pending cases, while the Ministry of Home Affairs had 24,409 cases.

title: Amit Shah-led high-level committee approves disaster mitigation projects
Text: A high-level committee headed by Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Thursday approved several disaster mitigation and capacity building projects for various states that include combating urban flooding and checking glacial lake outburst floods. The committee gave its nod to nine proposals for funding from National Disaster Mitigation Fund (NDMF) and National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF). Among the proposals approved include six projects in Telangana, Gujarat, Karnataka, West Bengal and Maharashtra at a total cost of Rs 2514.36 crore for urban floor management. Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. The six cities where the funds will be spent are Mumbai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad and Pune, according to an official statement.

title: Foreign investors pull out $ 1.27 billion from market after Budget
Text: Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) pulled out nearly $ 1.27 billion (around Rs 10,710 crore) from the stock market in the three days since the government raised taxes on derivatives trades and on capital gains from equity investments in the Union Budget. According to stock exchange data, FPIs sold equities worth Rs 2,975 crore on July 23 when the Budget was announced and another Rs 5,130 crore on July 24. They withdrew Rs 2,605 crore on Thursday. Advertisement On the other hand, domestic institutional investors had bought stocks worth around Rs 6,900 crore since July 23. The Sensex had fallen just 463 points to 80,039.80 after the Budget presentation, aided by domestic buying support.

title: In Laos, Wang & Jaishankar discuss ties
Text: India and China on Thursday discussed complete disengagement along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) at the earliest and normalcy in bilateral relations. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar met his Chinese counterpart Wang Yi on the sidelines of the ASEAN meetings in Vientiane, Laos, to review the situation and take forward the discussions held in their last meeting in Astana earlier this month, the Ministry of External Affairs said in a statement. “The meeting gave the two ministers an opportunity to review the situation since their last meeting at Astana on 4 July, 2024. Their talks focussed on finding an early resolution of the remaining issues along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) to stabilise and rebuild bilateral relations,” the statement said. Both ministers agreed on the need to work with purpose and urgency to achieve complete disengagement at the earliest.

title: Channi's reference to Amritpal triggers row in LS
Text: Congress leader Charanjit Singh Channi said Thursday that the detention of an elected MP under the NSA was part of an "undeclared emergency" by the Centre, drawing a sharp response from the Bharatiya Janata Party who said he was referring to jailed radical Sikh preacher Amritpal Singh. IMAGE: Congress MP Charanjit Singh Channi speaks in Lok Sabha. Photograph: Sansad TV/ANI Photo During a debate in Lok Sabha, the former Punjab chief minister referred to the recently concluded Lok Sabha elections and said, "This is also an emergency that a Member of Parliament elected by 20 lakh people in Punjab has been detained under the NSA (National Security Act) ... He is unable to speak about his constituency here (in Parliament). This is also an emergency." The Congress said views expressed by Channi "on Amritpal Singh" are his own and do not reflect in any way the position of the party. "The views expressed by Charanjit Singh Channi, MP on Amritpal Singh are his own, and do not reflect in any way the position of the Indian National Congress," Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh said in a post on X. While Channi did not name anyone, BJP leaders said

title: 'Jobs Have To Be Created Everywhere'
Text: 'I found it unbelievable that L&T said 45,000 jobs were waiting to be filled because of unavailability of suitable skillsets.' 'So, when the Opposition sweepingly says there are no jobs, I'm sorry... I'm not saying it's raining jobs, but there are jobs. The (skill) gap has to be bridged.' Illustration: Dominic Xavier/Rediff.com A day after presenting the Union Budget for 2024-2025, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman spoke to Shrimi Choudhary, Ruchika Chitravanshi, Asit Ranjan Mishra and Nivedita Mookerji/Business Standard on issues ranging from the private sector's role in job creation to coalition needs in making Budgets, at her North Block office. Was the seventh Budget your toughest yet? Can't say this was the toughest. In the July 2019 Budget, I hardly had any time to prepare as it was the start of the month. This time, the letter and spirit of the vote on account had to be subsumed in the Budget, and a lot of additions were made. But this is the first time you have had to deal with the challenges of a coalition... I did not feel any additional burden. There is challenge each time, in each Budget. We did Budget-making during COVID-19. What can be more difficult

title: MSME credit to ride Budget push, offset unsecured stress
Text: Synopsis To enhance credit flow to MSMEs, the government is urging banks to offer collateral-free term loans and additional support during financial stress. The FY25 budget includes a new credit guarantee scheme to help MSMEs in manufacturing secure loans for machinery and equipment without needing collateral or a third-party guarantee.

title: MP detained under NSA an emergency': Charanjit Singh Channi's reference to Amritpal Singh triggers row in Lok Sabha
Text: Synopsis Congress leader Charanjit Singh Channi claimed that the detention of an elected MP was an 'undeclared emergency' by the Centre, drawing criticism from BJP. The Congress distanced itself by saying Channi's views were personal. The article details a heated exchange in the Lok Sabha and Channi's criticism of the BJP government's policies and actions.

title: Hail-a-tax to catch a ride: Budget focuses on MSP assurance, tax adjustments sectoral reforms despite implementation challenges
Text: Synopsis The 2024 budget focuses on key stakeholders including the poor, women, youth, and farmers, aiming to address their needs through various initiatives. Highlights include the reiteration of a 50% margin over production cost for MSPs, though previously announced and now reaffirmed, drawing close scrutiny. Other sectors such as direct tax rates see adjustments, with reductions in short-term and long-term capital gains taxes, and adjustments to corporate tax rates for foreign entities.

title: Credit guarantee cover extended to ₹7.5 lakh under revamped Model Skill Loan Scheme
Text: A similar scheme launched in 2015 saw low fund utilisation because individual loans were limited to ₹1.5 lakh, though high-end skilling courses cost much more; new scheme also expands lender network to NBFCs, small banks Close on the heels of the Union Budget announcement hiking the eligible size of loans for high-end skilling courses under the Model Skill Loan scheme from ₹1.5 lakh to ₹7.5 lakh, Skill Development Minister Jayant Chaudhary launched the revamped scheme on Thursday. The earlier Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme for Skill Development, notified in November 2015 to create a credit guarantee fund for courses aligned to the National Skill Qualification Framework, faced multiple challenges. As on March 31, 2024, loans amounting to ₹115.75 crore had been extended to just 10,077 borrowers. Skill Development Ministry officials said that the low fund utilisation under the scheme over the past decade under the scheme was due to low ticket size of loans (upto ₹1.5 lakh), even as course costs and fees rose due to inflation, leaving many high-cost courses out of the scheme. “Only member lending institutes of the Indian Banking Association (IBA) were allowed to lend earlier, and there was low uptake by both private and public sector

title: 3 booked for duping film financer duped of Rs 2.61 crore
Text: Three people, including a self-proclaimed film director, were booked on Monday for allegedly defrauding a film financer of Rs 2.61 crore by inducing him to invest money in production of a film and offering him lucrative returns on the investment. On the complaint of the 52-year-old film financier, police have registered an FIR against Nilima Sharma, Rohit Sharma and Anisha Sharma, who allegedly committed the offence between November 2022 and March 2024. The complainant, who is an Andheri resident, has a civil contract company. He also has a business of producing films under the banner of Vishal Arts. Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. As per his complaint to the police, the three accused conspired together and in November 2022, sent Anisha to the complainant to get employment in his company. Police said this was done to get details of the financial condition of the complainant’s company. When the complainant discovered that Anisha gave false details regarding her previous employment, she was immediately sacked.

title: Tripura HC seeks report from state govt on rising HIV, AIDS cases; asks for details of initiatives
Text: With a rise in the number of HIV-positive and AIDS cases in the state, the Tripura High Court on Wednesday issued a notice to the state government seeking a report on the initiatives taken in this regard. The High Court registered a suo moto case based on the letter of the executive chairman of Legal Services Authority justice T Amarnath Goud written to Chief Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh where he mentioned about a hike in the HIV/AIDS cases and deaths among students at an alarming rate in the state. Goud attached figures of district-wise HIV cases to the letter. The notice was issued to the secretaries of the Education and Health departments, Government of India.

title: Maharashtra onion belt gets no relief in Union Budget, farmers vow repeat of LS poll blow to BJP
Text: The NDA which suffered a setback in the onion belt of Maharashtra in the recent Lok Sabha polls, winning only one of six seats – largely due to a ban on the export of the crop – could be in for more tears in the Assembly polls as traders and farmers expressed their disappointment with the Union Budget not lifting restrictions on the same. Admitting that prolonged restrictions on free export of onions is hurting the party’s prospects, a BJP leader in Nashik regretted: “Our leaders were not able to convince the party’s central leadership about the political effect of this.” Advertisement Dindori, Nashik, Beed, Aurangabad, Ahmednagar and Dhule Lok Sabha seats make up the onion belt of the state, which accounts for around 34% of the country’s onion production. Nashik alone accounts for over 40% of the state’s onion cultivation. Except Aurangabad, where Sandipan Bhumare of the Shiv Sena led by Eknath Shinde won, all these other seats were lost by the NDA. In Ahmednagar and Beed, relative newcomers like Nilesh Lanke and Bajranj Sonawane of the NCP (SP) trumped BJP stalwarts like Sujay Vikhe-Patil and Pankaja Munde, respectively.

title: Nitish Kumar ko gussa kyon aata hai? Bihar looks on as CM flies off the handle – again
Text: IN MARCH 2021, during the Budget Session of the Bihar Assembly, RJD MLA and dentist Mukesh Roshan arrived with a blood pressure machine to the House. He wanted to check Chief Minister Nitish Kumar as he was worried about him, Roshan told reporters. “The CM is losing his temper frequently. High blood pressure cannot be good for his health.” More than three years and much water under the bridge later – with Nitish making a flip to the RJD side and a flop back to the BJP, all the while staying on as CM – what hasn’t changed is the irascible mood of Nitish. This is quite a change for the man once known as the Mr Cool of Bihar, who created a distinct identity for himself, with his measured ways, among more colourful contemporaries such as Lalu Prasad, Sharad Yadav and Ram Vilas Paswan, among others. Advertisement On Wednesday, the Bihar Assembly was again witness to the angry Nitish, when he lashed out at RJD Masaurhi MLA Rekha Paswan, for interrupting him. At the time, the CM was trying to tell the House that his government intended to go to the Supreme Court against a High Court order staying

title: MUDA scam: Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah defends himself even as Leader of Opposition R Ashok calls him ‘coward’
Text: In the wake of continued protests by BJP legislators over the Mysuru Urban Development Authority (MUDA) scam, Chief Minister Siddaramaiah tried to clear his name off at the Legislative Council on Thursday by asking what his role was in the irregularities. Opposition parties, he said, are trying to tarnish his image which has “had no black marks” in a political career spanning 40 years. Amidst loud sloganeering by BJP and JD(S) MLCs, alleging irregularities by members of CM’s family in the scam, Siddaramaiah maintained that alternate sites were provided to his wife when the BJP was in power. He maintained that the MUDA had discretionary powers. “They acquired our land illegally and developed layouts. It later considered our application (regarding the land lost) and allotted alternate sites,” he said, adding that he had not demanded sites in any particular area.

title: Ghatkopar hoarding case: Cops launch search for crucial witness after he goes ‘missing’
Text: The Mumbai Police SIT has launched a search for Arshad Khan, who was summoned to record his statement for the second time in connection with the Ghatkopar hoarding collapse case but did not turn up. Khan’s statement is important as he had allegedly taken over Rs 50 lakhs from Ego Media Pvt Ltd, the company that operated the 140X120 feet hoarding that collapsed on a petrol pump in Ghatkopar killing 17 people on May 13. The SIT has already filed a first chargesheet against four people, including the owner of Ego Media Bhavesh Bhinde. An officer said, ” Khan did not turn up to record his statement. His mobile phone is switched off and we are not able to trace him. We have issued notices and our teams are on the lookout for him.” The officer added teams have been dispatched to various places in the country to look for him.

title: Manipur CM Biren Singh leaves for Delhi to attend NITI Aayog meeting, says will apprise PM Modi on state of violence
Text: Manipur Chief Minister N Biren Singh on Thursday left for New Delhi to join the NITI Aayog chief ministers’ meeting, which Prime Minister Narendra Modi will chair on Saturday, July 27. Before leaving Imphal, the chief minister interacted with the media on the sidelines of an outreach programme. Singh expressed his confidence that his visit to New Delhi may bring some positive outcomes while citing the 13 months of ethnic strife gripping the state. Singh added that he would meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi during the meeting and apprise him of the prevailing situation of Manipur. “I will request for an immediate solution to the present crisis. I am very optimistic and I hope something positive will come out of it,” Singh added.

title: BJP MP seeks Bharat Ratna for Kanshi Ram
Text: A BJP MP in Lok Sabha Thursday demanded the Bharat Ratna, the country’s highest civilian honour, for the iconic Dalit leader Kanshi Ram. Arun Kumar Sagar, who represents the SC-reserved Shahjahanpur constituency in Uttar Pradesh, hailed the late Bahujan Samaj Party founder as a “Bahujan Nayak” and social reformer who dedicated his life to the welfare of the downtrodden. “Considering his contribution to society and the nation, I appeal to the government to take appropriate action for honouring Kanshi Ram with the Bharat Ratna,” said Sagar, a two-time MP.

title: Curious case of Manoj Soni: UPSC chairman, who quit amid Puja Khedkar firestorm, no stranger to row
Text: At the Maharaja Sayajirao University (MSU) of Baroda, Vadodara, some of his former colleagues say they were getting “feelers” for some time that Dr Manoj Soni would not complete his tenure at the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC), although his sudden resignation from its top post came as a “surprise”. Soni, 59, has quit as the UPSC chairman citing “personal reasons”, even though his tenure would end in 2029. Considered close to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Soni joined the UPSC as its member on June 28, 2017 and took oath as its chairperson on May 16, 2023. An alumnus of the MSU where he did his BA and MA in Political Science in the 1980s, specialising in International Relations, Soni tendered his resignation as the UPSC chief about a month back, and “expects to be relieved by July 31”, a senior central government official told The Indian Express. “His (Soni’s) resignation is not at all connected with the current controversy surrounding the IAS probationer Puja Khedkar, and is only an unfortunate coincidence”, the official claimed. Advertisement Khedkar is facing a criminal case for faking her identity to fraudulently avail attempts in the civil services examination, which has triggered a massive

title: Congress distances itself from Channi’s comments on Amritpal Singh: ‘Do not reflect party’s position’
Text: A controversy erupted Thursday after Congress MP Charanjit Singh Channi said in Lok Sabha that the detention of an elected MP from Punjab under the National Security Act (NSA) was part of an “undeclared Emergency” by the Centre. His remark drew a sharp response from the BJP which said he was referring to Waris Punjab De chief Amritpal Singh, who is detained in Assam under the NSA. Advertisement During a debate on the Budget in Lok Sabha, the former Punjab chief minister, while accusing BJP of imposing an undeclared emergency, said: “An MP elected by 20 lakh people in Punjab has been detained under the NSA… He is unable to speak about his constituency. This is also an emergency.”

title: Infant tests positive for Chandipura virus in Gujarat’s Bharuch; patient from same village where 1st case was identified
Text: The number of positive cases of Chandipura Viral Encephalitis (CHPV) went up to 37 on Thursday in Gujarat, as more samples tested positive, a bulletin issued by the state government said. Meanwhile, Additional Director of the Gujarat Health Department Nilam Patel told ANI that 10 deaths have been confirmed due to the virus. At the same time, viral encephalitis has proven fatal to 44, of the total 124 patients reported so far, the bulletin stated. Bharuch’s Ghanikhut village has reported its second suspected Chandipura virus case after a 13-month-old boy turned up at a community health centre with symptoms of diarrhoea, high-grade fever and vomiting Wednesday.

title: Homes flooded, traffic hit, drains clogged as heavy rain lashes Gurgaon
Text: Gurgaon residents woke up to heavy rain on Thursday morning, which left several localities waterlogged and threw traffic out of gear on key stretches, including the Mehrauli-Gurgaon road. Visuals from various parts of the city showed people and vehicles wading through knee-deep water in various stretches. Till 8 am, Gurgaon tehsil received 2 mm of rain while Wazirabad recorded rainfall of 83 mm. Officials of the Gurugram Metropolitan Development Authority (GMDA) said waterlogging was reported in Sectors 42, 43, 44, 55 and 56. Teams were deployed with pumps and the water was cleared in two hours, it said. A GMDA spokesperson said, “Teams are on the ground at different locations in the city to support quick discharge of stormwater. Pumpsets have been deployed at hotspots such as Narsinghpur, Khandsa Chowk, Rajiv Chowk, Sector 67 as well as on Ghata road to help remove any waterlogging on the carriageway. A tree along IFFCO Chowk fell with impact and damaged the drain; a team is working on rectifying the issue. There was heavy rainfall on Golf Course Road this morning and the creeks and ponds developed by GMDA proved beneficial in carrying the stormwater and preventing flooding on the stretch.”

title: Make public video clips of my alleged remarks against Pawar, Uddhav: Deshmukh dares Fadnavis
Text: Senior NCP (SP) leader Anil Deshmukh on Thursday challenged Deputy Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis to make public the video clips that show him allegedly speaking against NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar and Shiv Sena (UBT) president Uddhav Thackeray. Addressing a press conference here, Deshmukh said, “Yesterday, Fadnavis claimed that he has some video clips about my comments against Sharad Pawar and Uddhav Thackeray. Then he should make the video clips public because I know he possesses none.” “But he does not have any such video clips and he talked about them just to level allegations,” he said. Deshmukh also showed a pen drive saying that it contains evidence about the allegations he made against Fadnavis.

title: Q1 results: Adani Green profits up by nearly 95%, Nestle India posts slowest revenue growth in 8 years
Text: Adani Green Energy profit up nearly 95% to Rs 629 crore in Q1 Adani Green Energy posted nearly a 95 per cent rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 629 crore for the June quarter, on the back of higher revenues. The company reported Rs 323 crore consolidated net profit for the quarter that ended on June 30, a BSE filing showed. Total income rose to Rs 3,122 crore in the quarter from Rs 2,550 crore in the same period a year ago. Adani Green Energy CEO Amit Singh said in the statement, “Adani Green is well on track to achieve its 2030 capacity target of 50 GW, including at least 5 GW energy storage, in the form of pumped hydro, with sites already secured and clear visibility on evacuation.” Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. Canara Bank Q1 net profit up 10 pc to Rs 3,905 crore State-owned Canara Bank posted a 10 per cent rise in its net profit to Rs 3,905 crore for the first quarter that ended June 30, on account of reduction in bad loans. The Bengaluru-based lender had earned a net profit of Rs 3,535 crore in the year-ago period. During the

title: Karnataka government relents to Opposition demand, refers Greater Bengaluru Governance Bill to House committee
Text: The Karnataka government on Thursday conceded to Opposition demands to refer the Greater Bengaluru Governance Bill to a House committee before seeking passage in the Legislative Assembly. The Bill was cleared by the Cabinet on Monday and was tabled in the Assembly a day later. Deputy Chief Minister and Bengaluru Development Minister D K Shivakumar, who rose to seek a discussion on the Bill, said that the reforms proposed in the legislation were required for the better administration of Bengaluru. Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. Leader of Opposition R Ashok sought that the government form a House committee of MLAs and MLCs to deliberate on the Bill before placing it in the Assembly. “The Bill should be kept pending,” he demanded, saying that it was drafted only by officials without wider consultations. BJP MLA S T Somashekar suggested that all MLAs and MLCs from Bengaluru be included in the committee.

title: Bengaluru man steals bikes to fund cancer treatment of friend’s wife, arrested
Text: The Bengaluru police on Wednesday announced the arrest of a 30-year-old man who allegedly turned to stealing two-wheelers to support his friend’s wife undergoing breast cancer treatment. The police said the accused, Ashok, was living at his friend’s house after he had been separated from his wife. The Girinagar police in Bengaluru also arrested his accomplice, Satish alias Sathya, 34, and recovered eight bikes worth Rs 10.71 lakh. The police said when Ashok learned that his friend’s wife was suffering from cancer and couldn’t afford treatment, he initially tried to borrow money from many people but couldn’t secure enough for the treatment.

title: Water recedes from parts of Surat city after rain stops; people start leaving shelter homes
Text: With no rain on Wednesday night and Thursday morning in Surat, water has started receding from parts of the city in Gujarat and over 955 people have started returning from shelter homes. Owing to heavy rain received in the past two days, over 132 roads to different villages were closed. These roads included 12 in Umarpada, 27 in Mangrol, 21 in Mandvi, five in Mahuva, 29 in Bardoli, 16 in Palsana, four in Choryasi, 15 in Olpad, and three roads in Kamrej. Since Thursday morning, some of these roads have been reopened for the public. Waterlogging and the overflow of creek water meant that several areas in the city such as Udhna, Limbayat, Sarthana and Sachin were flooded. As water entered residential societies, over 955 people, including women, children and elderly people, were rescued by teams from the municipal corporation and shifted to shelter homes set up at community health centres and schools on Wednesday.

title: Cows no longer be called ‘strays’ in Rajasthan: Minister
Text: Rajasthan’s Gopalan Minister Joraram Kumawat Wednesday announced that cows will no longer be called strays in the state. Kumawat, who is also the minister for Animal Husbandry and Dairy, said that from now on stray bovines will be called nirashrit (destitute) in the state. Replying to a debate on the grant demand of Animal Husbandry and Fisheries Department in the Rajasthan Assembly on Wednesday night, Kumawat said that “the cow, which we consider as our mother, and Nandi (bull), which is Lord Shiva’s vehicle, we cannot call them as strays.” Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. He said that it is right that the spoken word ‘stray’ got printed (in the budget) “but I declare in this House that it will be written everywhere that the cow progeny is besahara or nirashrit instead of stray.”

title: Action taken in 3 booth capturing complaints in 2024 polls: EC
Text: The Election Commission (EC) has received 925 complaints regarding booth capturing during the 2024 Lok Sabha and state Assembly polls, but disposed of all but three of them since the rest were found false or unsubstantiated, the Law Ministry told Rajya Sabha Thursday. In response to a question by Shiv Sena MP Priyanka Chaturvedi about complaints of booth capturing, Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal provided the EC’s information on the number of complaints and action taken. Action was taken in one complaint in Arunachal Pradesh during the simultaneous Lok Sabha and state assembly elections in the state, in which two people were arrested. A repoll was conducted and an FIR lodged at the Khenewa police station of East Kameng district, the reply said.

title: Heavy rains disrupt public transport, over 60 local train services cancelled
Text: The public transport system in Mumbai faced severe disruptions on Thursday due to the intense rain across the city. Local train services under both Central and Western Railways were significantly impacted. The Central Railway had to cancel over 60 local train services, with trains running on an average 30 minutes behind schedule during the afternoon hours. In the evening hour at 6 pm, a rail fracture was reported between Ghatkopar and Vikhroli on the up direction towards CSMT. A CR official said that track safety was assured at 6.20 with trains allowed to run at 30kmph speed. On Western Railway, while local services remained operational, long-distance trains originating from places like Baroda experienced delays, subsequently affecting the scheduled local services. Some 10-12 trains were cancelled as a result, but not due to rains, said a WR official.

title: If Fadnavis has audio and video clips, he should take action instead of issuing plain threats: Nana Patole
Text: The Bharatiya Janata Party government is extensively using Central agencies like ED, CBI and the Income Tax department to eliminate opponents, state Congress president Nana Patole said on Thursday. Those who accepted the BJP’s offer became ‘pure,’ and those who refused were acted upon through these agencies and jailed, he alleged. “Deputy CM Devendra Fadnavis is threatening to expose audio and video clips of the opposition. Why is Fadnavis, who holds the home portfolio, not taking action if he has such clips instead of issuing plain threats,” Patole asked. Speaking to media persons in Nagpur, the Congress state president said that Ravindra Waikar, a leader of Uddhav Thackeray’s Shiv Sena, mentioned that he had to change his party out of compulsion after his candidacy was announced. Eknath Shinde and his colleagues are under BJP’s wings due to ED’s intimidation, and the same experiment might have been done with former Home Minister Anil Deshmukh, who is revealing these things, he alleged.

title: Lok Sabha briefly adjourned as spat between MoS and Channi gets personal
Text: Lok Sabha was adjourned for more than 30 minutes Thursday after an argument between Congress member Charanjit Singh Channi and BJP’s Ravneet Singh Bittu, a Minister of State, got personal. Remarks from both members were expunged later. Channi, who was participating in a discussion on the Union Budget, referred to the assassination of Bittu’s grandfather, former Punjab chief minister Beant Singh. Bittu, who recently quit the Congress to join the BJP, responded: “My grandfather sacrificed his life for the country and not for the Congress.” Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. The Minister of State for Railways and Food Processing Industries then made some personal remarks against Channi, triggering anger among Congress members.

title: Woman student stabbed by ex-student on Malda varsity campus
Text: A man in his early twenties allegedly stabbed a woman student on the campus of the Gour Banga University in Malda district on Thursday and then tried to kill himself with the same knife, police said. Both of them have been admitted to Malda Medical College and their condition is said to be critical, police added. “We are looking into the incident. The motive isn’t clear yet. However, primary facie, the accused knew the woman student,” said a police officer. Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. The knife used in the attack has been recovered, the officer added. The incident took place when the classes were going on. It is alleged that the accused, who is a former student of the university, stabbed the woman student in the corridor while she was on her way to attend classes. The woman is a student of mathematics.

title: INDIA bloc rally on Jul 30 over Kejriwal’s declining health in jail: AAP
Text: The INDIA bloc of opposition parties will hold a rally on July 30 at the Jantar Mantar here to raise the issue of Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal’s declining health inside the Tihar, the AAP said on Thursday. The Aam Aadmi Party has been accusing the BJP of “conspiring to kill” Kejriwal in jail and cited his medical report to show that his sugar levels had fallen 26 times between June 3 and July 7. The party, a constituent of the INDIA bloc, has been accusing the BJP-led central government and Lt Governor V K Saxena of playing with Kejriwal’s life. Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. “The INDIA bloc will hold a big rally at Jantar Mantar on July 30 to raise the issue of Kejriwal’s falling health,” the AAP said.

title: Punjab won’t withdraw free electricity schemes, CM Bhagwant Mann makes it clear; govt chalks out long-term plan to rationalise subsidies
Text: Unlike the neighbouring state of Himachal Pradesh, which had withdrawn the power subsidy given to the people in order to get financial help from the 16th Finance Commission, Punjab said it will continue to give free electricity to the agriculture sector and up to 300 free units of power to the domestic sector. Sources in the government said Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann has made it clear that he would not touch the power subsidy. “He has said that this has to continue. There is no bailout. We have to think of other ways to lessen the burden of subsidy on the state exchequer,” the source added. In fact, Punjab Finance Minister Harpal Cheema had on Wednesday said the free electricity schemes will continue. Advertisement Meanwhile, Punjab has prepared an ambitious rationalisation plan under which 80 per cent of the agriculture power feeders and 100 per cent of the domestic power feeders will be powered by solar energy by 2047. The government has also chalked out a plan to solarise all institutional and industrial buildings by 2031. Notably, the incumbent Aam Aadmi Party’s (AAP) term will come to an end in March 2027 unless it is re-elected in the 2027 Assembly

title: Bengaluru court cites Charles Sobraj case, refuses to allow actor Darshan Thoogudeepa access to home-cooked food
Text: A local court in Bengaluru on Thursday, while denying Kannada film actor Darshan Thoogudeepa’s plea to get home cooked food, cited a Supreme Court order in serial killer Charles Sobraj’s case and said no fundamental rights can be extended to the citizen without reasonable restriction. Turning down the plea, the court said that it cannot provide relaxation for someone who is arrested in a murder case and added that doing so will be against Rule 728 of the Karnataka Prisons and Correctional Services Manual (KPCSM)- 2021. Kannada film star Darshan Thoogudeepa and others have been arrested in connection with the murder of Renukaswamy, a resident of Chitradurga. Darshan, who is presently in judicial custody, had sought home cooked food stating that he lost weight and was suffering from stomach ache due to lack of high protein food. Raking up Article 21 Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. Darshan’s counsel had argued that Article 21 (the Right to Life and Personal Liberty) of the Indian Constitution guarantees the fundamental rights to every citizen and the same is also applicable to the prisoners who are lodged in prisons. In support of his arguments, he also cited the Charles Sobraj vs

title: With their ‘tu-tu, main-main’, Channi, Bittu put Punjab in Parliament limelight
Text: Country, party, property and poverty — these words kept flying thick and fast as Jalandhar MP Charanjit Singh Channi and Union Minister of State Ravneet Singh Bittu had a verbal duel in Parliament on Thursday. It all started when Channi while speaking on the Budget suddenly addressed the MoS, “Bittu ji, your grandfather (former Punjab chief minister Beant Singh who was assassinated on August 31, 1995, in a suicide bombing attack) was martyred. He didn’t die on that day but he died on the day when you left Congress.” Advertisement During the Lok Sabha election campaign, Bittu was dubbed a traitor by Congress leaders, a charge made in Parliament on Thursday as well. A three-time Congress MP, he had switched to the BJP in March this year ahead of the polls. He contested on the BJP ticket from Ludhiana but lost to the Congress’s Amrinder Singh Raja Warring.

title: As Oppn CMs announce boycott of NITI Aayog meet, Mamata postpones Delhi visit by a day
Text: West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee on Thursday postponed her visit to Delhi for the NITI Aayog meeting from Thursday to Friday. The meeting itself is to be held on Saturday, July 27. Advertisement Banerjee’s decision, according to sources in her party Trinamool Congress, comes a day after state chief ministers from the opposition INDIA bloc, such as Tamil Nadu CM M K Stalin, decided to boycott the NITI Aayog meeting. The objective of their boycott is to protest the central government’s alleged discrimination in terms of funds allocation for opposition-ruled states in this year’s union budget. “The Chief Minister will not be going to New Delhi today. She didn’t disclose any reason for her decision,” said a TMC source. The TMC is also part of the INDIA bloc.

title: No wages, harsh conditions, little food: Jharkhand labourers recount ordeal after return from Cameroon
Text: After a couple of months of working deep in the forests of Cameroon, even in the pouring rain, 45-year-old Makund Mahato from Jharkhand saw another worker, from a different country, fall to his death when the land they were working on caved in. “He could have been saved… This hit us hard, and we started demanding our salaries. The contractor promised us money every other day, but kept putting it off,” he said. Advertisement He was among 27 labourers from different parts of Jharkhand who returned home Wednesday after being stuck in Cameroon for months. In search of a better livelihood, the 27 had left their homes in Bokaro, Giridih, and Hazaribagh districts in the third week of March, and reached Cameroon in West Africa. They were hired to install electricity transmission towers.

title: Opposition calls out ‘Andhra-Bihar’ skew in Budget, Kangana delivers maiden speech: Key highlights from Parliament
Text: Accusations continued to fly thick and fast on Thursday, the fourth day of the Budget session, with Opposition parties claiming that the Union Budget is heavily skewed in favour of states ruled by BJP allies, particularly Andhra Pradesh and Bihar. This contention ignited fierce debate and disorder. Opposition MPs have taken to the floor with fervour, labelling the Budget as “discriminatory.” They argue it overlooks the pressing needs of regions not aligned with the ruling NDA. Kerala’s Congress MP Hibi Eden likened the government’s approach to “operating on two ventilators,” alluding to crises in Manipur and ongoing farmer protests while highlighting Kerala’s economic struggles. Advertisement 📌Voices of Critique Congress MP Charanjit Singh Channi vehemently criticised the Budget for its lack of provisions for Punjab, dubbing it an “undeclared emergency.” He noted the absence of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman during crucial discussions, suggesting a lack of seriousness about the issues at hand. “This budget will not save the country; it will only save the NDA government,” he asserted, stressing the dire situation in Punjab amid floods and a drug crisis. TMC MP Sougata Roy echoed these sentiments, branding it an “Andhra-Bihar Budget.” He accused the government

title: Madhya Pradesh school principal booked for ‘stopping students from reciting Sanskrit verses’
Text: The principal of a convent school in Madhya Pradesh’s Guna district has been booked for allegedly stopping some students from reciting a Sanskrit verse and forcing them to speak in English, police said. title: JU student ‘suffers panic attack’, hospitalised; university says not a case of ragging
Text: A Jadavpur University (JU) student suffered a panic attack after he was allegedly questioned by a group of students over a missing laptop, officials at the varsity said. The first-year post-graduate computer science student was admitted to a hospital on Wednesday night and his condition is said to be stable now. Ruling out ragging, the university administration said the student was not beaten up. Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. “It was a case of misunderstanding between some students regarding a stolen laptop. The student got scared and suffered a panic attack. He is completely fine now and will be discharged from the hospital soon. We also told him that if he faces any problem regarding his study, then he should approach us. The student was not beaten up. It is not a case of ragging,” Snehamanju Basu, the registrar of the university, told mediapersons.

Text: An Indian man who has said he was duped into fighting for the Russian side in the war against Ukraine has again appealed to the Indian government to help him return home. Friends and family of Urgen Tamang (47), who is from Kalimpong in West Bengal, have also written to Russia President Vladimir Putin on his behalf, explaining his situation and asking for help. title: ‘Want to see same level of action against anti-India elements’: MEA on Canada charging 2 people over threats to Trudeau
Text: India on Thursday called upon Canada to take action against anti-India elements. “We expect Canada to take action against anti-India elements who have repeatedly threatened Indian leaders, institutions, airlines and diplomats by violence,” the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said. Addressing a media briefing, Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that he was aware of reports that Canada has charged two persons for online threats posed to PM Justin Trudeau but such actions are missing in case of those threatening Indian leaders and diplomats. “We have seen these reports. When a democracy adopts different yardsticks to measure or implement the rule of law and freedom of expression, it only exposes its own double standard,” he said.
