title: Gujarat heavy rainfall: Creeks flooded, 955 relocated in Surat
Text: The Surat Municipal Corporation (SMC) shifted 955 people to safer places in Surat city on Wednesday due to creeks flooding following heavy rainfall. Between 6 am to 6 pm on Wednesday, Surat received 314 mm of rainfall, resulting in waterlogging in different parts of the city. According to the SMC flood control room, while the water level at Kakra creek has reached 6.6 m, Bhedwad creek is at 6.8 m, Mithi Creek at 9 m, Bhatena Creek at 6.6 m and Simada creek at 4.5 m. The water level at these creeks are close to their danger marks, said civic officials. Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. SMC Commissioner Shalini Agrawal on Wednesday paid a visit to the creeks to review the situation.

title: Rs 362 crore given to 4 lakh Sahara depositors: Amit Shah
Text: Cooperation Minister Amit Shah Wednesday informed Rajya Sabha that Rs 362.91 crore has been disbursed to over 4.2 lakh depositors of Sahara Group of Cooperative Societies as of July 16 this year. In a written reply, Shah said this disbursement is facilitated through the CRCS-Sahara Refund Portal, which was established following a Supreme Court order on March 29, 2023, aimed at assisting legitimate depositors in reclaiming their funds. Presently, the payment of only up to Rs 10,000 is being disbursed to each genuine depositor against verified claims through an Aadhaar-linked bank account. “An amount of Rs 362.91 crore has been released to 4,20,417 depositors of Sahara Group of Cooperative Societies as on July 16, 2024,” he said.

title: Nine killed as torrential rain continues in Gujarat
Text: Nine people were killed and hundreds shifted to safety on Wednesday, as torrential rain continued to lash various parts of Gujarat. According to a statement issued by the government, while three persons died at Devbhumi Dwarka, two each died at Banaskantha and Kutch and one each at Rajkot and Surat. The deaths occurred due to lighting strike and flooding, it added. Till 6 pm on Wednesday, Gujarat has received 461.22 mm of rainfall, which is 52.33 per cent of the total average rainfall it receives in the season. Kutch has received maximum rainfall at 75.50 mm, followed by Saurashtra (73.36%), south Gujarat (62.04%), east and central Gujarat (31.38%) and north Gujarat (31.38%).

title: Rehabilitate those affected by anti-encroachment drive: SC to Uttarakhand
Text: The Supreme Court Wednesday said that authorities should identify and devolve a scheme for those who are likely to be affected by the drive to evict encroachers in Uttarakhand’s Haldwani. The court asked Uttarakhand Chief Secretary to convene a meeting in this regard with railway authorities and the Union Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. “As the first initiative, let the land, which is required immediately (for Railways development) be identified with full description. Similarly, the families who are likely to be affected in the event of taking possession of that land also be immediately identified,” a three-judge bench presided by Justice Surya Kant said and directed that the exercise be completed in four weeks time.

title: Modi govt is on borrowed time, it will implode soon, says Abhishek Banerjee
Text: Trinamool Congress leader Abhishek Banerjee Wednesday claimed Prime Minister Narendra Modi is leading a “creaky, shaky and vulnerable” coalition government that is running on borrowed time. Taking part in the Budget discussion in Lok Sabha, he said the government was looking after the interests of only two states, ignoring all other citizens. “Waqt badal gaya (times have changed). Prime Minister Narendra Modi leads a creaky, shaky NDA coalition government, waiting to blow up. Rather than investing in the future of the country, it is unfortunate that the Union government is investing in Modiji’s political survival at the expense of the nation’s well-being,” said the MP from Diamond Harbour.

title: Does the right to be forgotten include taking down verdict? Supreme Court to decide
Text: Will the right to be forgotten include taking down judgments that reveal an acquitted person’s identity? The Supreme Court Wednesday said it will decide. “We will have to settle the law,” said CJI D Y Chandrachud, presiding over a three-judge bench, which was hearing an appeal by Indian Kanoon, a law search engine. The portal had moved SC against a March 3, 2024 Madras High Court direction asking it to take down a judgment copy in a sexual assault case as it had the name of the accused who was finally acquitted. The man had moved High Court saying he was denied Australian citizenship because his name appeared in the judgment.

title: Alcohol test similar to those for flight crew among steps to curb accidents involving cluster buses
Text: Taking cues from the pre-flight drug and alcohol testing for pilots and cabin crew members in the aviation industry, the Delhi Integrated Multi-Modal Transit System Limited (DIMTS) is set to conduct random testing of drivers and conductors of cluster buses for alcohol consumption before the allocation of the duty roster, officials said. The move comes after a 55-year-old woman was killed and 23 passengers were injured when a DTC bus rammed into a Metro pillar in West Delhi’s Punjab Bagh. The directions were issued in a meeting on Tuesday held by the DIMTS to discuss the accident. The meeting was attended by all the cluster bus providers, depot managers, and regional managers to deliberate upon the accidents and discuss a slew of measures to prevent such incidents from happening again, said officials. “Random testing was done earlier also but it was done in the night and second shifts…But now, the DIMTS has decided to conduct daily checks in the morning shift before the driver and conductor get onboard for their shift,” said a senior DIMTS official. “Apart from this, random or surprise checks will also be conducted during duty. Directions have been issued to all depot managers and cluster providers

title: BJP: Opposition looks negatively towards backward states
Text: NEW DELHI: BJP on Wednesday slammed Congress and other opposition parties for criticising the Union budget , saying that it revealed their political frustration and negative attitude towards "some backward states " that need special focus and assistance for development.BJP spokesperson and former Rajya Sabha MP G V L Narasimha Rao said Prime Minister Narendra Modi-led govt's Budget has been welcomed by "one and all" but the opposition parties are coming out with "immature and negative reactions" against it.Party's reaction comes against the backdrop of Congress and other constituents of the opposition INDIA bloc accusing govt of presenting a "discriminatory" Budget towards opposition-ruled states after finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman made a host of budgetary announcements for Andhra Pradesh and Bihar on Tuesday.JD(U) and TDP, which rule Bihar and Andhra Pradesh respectively, are key constituents of BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) govt at the Centre."The entire country looks at this as a progressive, pro-people, pro-poor, pro-farmer and pro-employement budget. It is a Budget which has actually laid out a vision for 'Viksit Bharat'," Rao said at a press conference.With more than Rs 48 lakh crore overall budgetary expenditure, the Union Budget 2024-25 has kept its focus on every section of the

title: Brakes of economy have fallen off but govt's horn keeps getting louder: Shashi Tharoor
Text: Asserting that the Union Budget in many ways is emblematic of the government's "economic mismanagement and financial recklessness", Congress leader Shashi Tharoor on Wednesday said the brakes of the Indian economy have fallen off but this government's horn keeps getting louder.Tharoor claimed that the government had been an underachiever despite setting high targets announced for Make in India."This government thinks that rhetoric is a substitute for action," the Congress leader said.He asserted that India is not spending enough on a crucial sector such as healthcare while other BRICS countries were spending 14-15 times more than it.This budget makes it abundantly clear that the BJP has run out of ideas, Tharoor said. Show more Show less

title: Budget 2024: INDIA bloc leaders hold protest against Modi govt at Parliament premises
Text: The INDIA bloc leaders staged protest against the new Union budget in the Parliament premises on July 24. The opposition parties have alleged Union Budget 2024 to be a "discriminatory budget”. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman presented her record seventh consecutive Union Budget 2024-25 on July 23, during the Budget Session of Parliament and made major announcements for Bihar and Andhra Pradesh, including a boost in infrastructure and special financial support. Show more Show less

title: Congress party has done nothing in 55 years: Maharashtra BJP chief Chandrashekhar Bawankule
Text: Synopsis Maharashtra BJP president Chandrashekhar Bawankule criticised the Congress for their negative remarks on the Union Budget, calling them "nautanki" and accusing them of deceiving voters for 55 years. He defended the Budget's alignment with PM Modi's promises, asserting it will lead to a developed India. Bawankule also warned of potential opposition halting government schemes if they win the state assembly elections. The budget focussed on economic growth and opportunities, with key priorities in agriculture, employment, and skilling.

title: Customs duty structure review to focus on reducing number of rates: Revenue Secy
Text: The government is looking at bringing down the number of customs duty levies to five from about a dozen presently, as part of the duty rationalisation exercise, Revenue Secretary Sanjay Malhotra said on Wednesday. The reduction in the number of customs rates will help reduce classification disputes, he said when asked about the Budget proposal for a comprehensive review of the rate structure in six months. On Tuesday, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in her Budget speech said the government will undertake a comprehensive review of the customs rate structure over the next six months to rationalise and simplify it for ease of trade, removal of duty inversion and reduction of disputes.

title: 10% reservation for ex-Agniveers in CAPFs, Assam Rifles: Govt
Text: The government has decided to reserve 10 per cent of vacancies in the Central Armed Police Forces and Assam Rifles for ex-Agniveers, the Rajya Sabha was informed Wednesday. A provision has been made for relaxation in the upper age limit and exemption from the Physical Efficiency Test in the recruitment to the post of constable (general duty) and rifleman in the CAPFs and Assam Rifles for ex-Agniveers, Minister of State for Home Affairs Nityanand Rai said in response to a written question. “The number of vacancies as of July 1, 2024, in the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) and Assam Rifles (AR) is 84,106 against a total sanctioned strength of 10,45,751,” he said. Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. Rai said the ministry has been taking and will continue to take earnest steps to fill up the vacancies expeditiously through the Union Public Service Commission, Staff Selection Commission and the forces concerned. “Time taken in the medical examination has been reduced to expedite the recruitment. Cut-off marks for shortlisting candidates for constable/GD has been lowered to get sufficient candidates (especially in categories where shortfalls have been observed),” he said. The minister said 67,345 people have been recruited between

title: 2 school buses carrying students ‘held up’ at police lines in UP, ARTO faces action
Text: The Uttar Pradesh government has initiated disciplinary proceedings against an assistant regional transport officer (ARTO) for allegedly holding up two school buses carrying students at the police lines in Chitrakoot district for nearly two hours, officials said. The government also suspended a regional inspector of the Transport Department over delay in issuing fitness certificates to the school buses, it is learnt. The buses transporting students from an inter college were impounded on Tuesday by a team led by Assistant Regional Transport Officer (Enforcement) Vivek Kumar Shukla since their fitness certificates had expired, the officials said. Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. The buses were taken to the police lines nearly 10 kilometres away and remained there from 11:15 am to 1:05 pm.

title: Lucknow hospital owner ‘assaulted’ by kin of patient who died during treatment
Text: A group of persons, reportedly relatives of a patient who passed away during treatment at a private hospital in Lucknow, allegedly assaulted the owner of the medical facility, holding him responsible for the death. A video of the incident is also doing rounds on social media. Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Anshu Jain said an FIR has been filed against unidentified persons in connection with the incident and an investigation is underway. Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. The complainant, Dr Ravi Dev, runs a hospital in Gomti Nagar Extension in the city. The police said they are examining the videos of the incident to identify those who assaulted the doctor. The complainant claimed that he did not know the people who attacked him.

title: Nita Ambani secures second term as International Olympic Committee member
Text: Nita Ambani, founder of Reliance Foundation, has been re-elected unanimously to the International Olympic Committee (IOC) for a second term. The announcement came on Wednesday, just days before the opening ceremony of the Paris Olympics. Ambani, the first Indian woman to join the IOC in 2016, expressed her gratitude for the renewed trust placed in her, saying she was “deeply honoured”. “I would like to thank President Bach and all my colleagues in the IOC for their faith and trust in me. This re-election is not just a personal milestone but also a recognition of India’s growing influence in the global sporting arena,” she said.

title: Maharashtra gets budget allocation of Rs 15,900 crore for railway development
Text: Maharashtra has been given a budget allocation of Rs 15,940 crore for railway works, Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said. He said that 41 projects covering the 5,877-km rail network worth Rs 81,580 crore are currently underway in the state. Among the key initiatives is the redevelopment of 128 stations in Maharashtra under the Amrit Bharat Station scheme. Additionally, the state has achieved 100% railway electrification and 180 km of new tracks are being laid annually. Vaishnaw noted that the total railway investment in the state stands at Rs 1.3 lakh crore, with significant funds allocated for various projects in this year’s budget. Addition of local train services: Mumbai’s suburban railway network, which operates 3,213 trains daily, is set to see a significant boost. Currently, 1,819 local trains run on the Central Railway and 1,394 on the Western Railway, serving 40 lakh and 35 lakh passengers, respectively. Under the Mumbai Urban Transport Project (MUTP), the 5th and 6th railway tracks between Kurla and CSMT will be laid to provide separate routes for local and mail-express trains. This project, along with the addition of 250 new local trains over the next five years, aims to remove congestion and improve travel comfort for

title: BJP councillor arrested in connection with SP worker’s killing in UP’s Gonda
Text: A BJP councillor has been arrested following an encounter with police in connection with the murder case of a Samajwadi Party (SP) worker in Uttar Pradesh’s Gonda district, officials said on Wednesday. Superintendent of Police Vineet Jaiswal said SP worker Om Prakash Singh (45), a resident of Mohalla Raja Tola in Parsapur town, was killed in broad daylight on Friday. A murder case was registered against five people, including Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) councillor Udaybhan Singh alias Lallan Sing and his three sons, following a complaint from the victim’s wife. The officer said police had already arrested two accused — Chandan Singh and Rohit — in the case, but the main accused, Udaybhan Singh, was absconding. Police had announced a reward of Rs 25,000 on information leading to his arrest.

title: Bengal BJP chief asks PM to make north Bengal a part of North East, TMC calls it ‘secessionist move’
Text: BJP’s West Bengal unit president Sukanta Majumdar on Wednesday said he has urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to incorporate northern parts of the state into the North East region since the two have “many similarities”. This triggered a strong reaction from the ruling TMC in the state, which called the BJP “secessionist”, accusing it of trying to divide West Bengal for its political benefit. In a video statement issued from Delhi, Majumdar, who is also Union Minister of State for Education, said, “I met with the Prime Minister and handed over a presentation highlighting the similarities between north Bengal and North East states. I requested him to incorporate north Bengal, a part of West Bengal, into the North East (states).” Advertisement “The Prime Minister will decide on the proposal in due time. If North Bengal is incorporated into the North East, it will benefit from the Central government schemes. There will be more development. I do not think the state government will have objections and will cooperate,” Majumdar, an MP from Balurghat in north Bengal, added. In the recent past, BJP leaders and MPs have raised the demand of a separate state of North Bengal to be carved out from

title: Months before polls, BMC opens gates for financial aid scheme for persons with disabilites
Text: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has started accepting applications for the Dharmaveer Anand Dighe Divyang Financial Assistance scheme, which seeks to provide half-yearly financial assistance ranging from Rs 6,000 to Rs 18,000 to nearly 60,000 persons with disabilities over the course of next five years. The move months ahead of Assembly elections in the state, slated for October. Named after Chief Minister Eknath Shinde’s mentor Anand Dighe, the scheme had been announced by the civic body in its fiscal budget 2024 – 2025, under which an allocation of Rs 111.83 crore for persons with physical disabilities had been made. Advertisement As a part of the scheme, the BMC is slated to provide financial assistance to nearly 60,000 disabled persons (UDID card holders), who are above the age of 18 years and permanent residents of Mumbai.

title: After Hathras stampede, UP Police comes up with SOP for crowd management: prepare in advance, Gazetted officer or local magistrate to be event in-charge
Text: To prevent incidents of stampede, the Uttar Pradesh Police has issued a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for crowd and police management at large events. This comes after a stampede at a religious congregation in Hathras on July 2 left 121 people dead. The SOP covers four main areas: continuous action to be taken in view of the crowd-caused disaster; advance preparations for events; emergency actions during a stampede; and overall event management. As per the SOP, a Gazetted officer or local magistrate will be appointed as the event in-charge. “All police, PAC, CAPF, and fire officers on duty will receive proper briefings. The use of public address systems, loudhailers, and other communication tools will activate the deployed forces. Adequate fire-fighting arrangements will be made, and vigilance will be maintained to monitor rumor mongers and anti-social elements,” the SOP stated.

title: 23 of total 118 suspected CHPV patients test positive so far
Text: of the 118 suspected cases of Chandipura Acute Viral Encephalitis (CHPV) reported in Gujarat so far, 23 people have tested positive since the outbreak of the disease, said a state government statement on Wednesday. The state has also reported a total of 41 deaths of suspected and positive cases. The highest number of confirmed CHPV positive cases have been reported from Sabarkantha and Panchmahal districts at three each. Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. At five deaths, maximum fatality has been reported from Panchmahal district, followed by Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation reporting four deaths and Aravalli, Morbi, Rajkot and Banaskantha with three deaths each. The state government also said that currently a total of 54 suspected CHPV cases have been admitted for viral encephalitis in the state while 23 have been discharged. In addition to the cases from the state, two patients each from Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh and one suspected CHPV case from Maharashtra are currently undergoing treatment in Gujarat.

title: 50-yr-old man, convicted in rape case earlier, arrested for raping 3-year-old
Text: A 50-year-old man has been arrested from Madhya Pradesh for allegedly raping a 3-year-old girl in Gurgaon, police said. The accused, identified as Ratan who hails from Balihari in Madhya Pradesh, had previously served a 10-year sentence for raping a 5-year-old girl, officials added. He was wanted in two other rape cases. Police said they have contacted other state police for information on unsolved cases. The case was registered at a police station in Gurgaon on April 26 after a woman lodged a complaint that she and her husband worked as labourers. Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. The accused had come to the site where they worked. He slept outside their room the previous night.

title: No felling of trees on Kanwar Marg, UP Govt to NGT
Text: Denying the allegations about illegal felling of trees, Uttar Pradesh government Wednesday said that the width of the proposed road of 20 meters, at some places, has been reduced to 15 meters to minimise the felling of trees. “No illegal activity of cutting unauthorised trees shall be done by the department as environment protection is the duty of state…Nearly 3,000 trees have been saved from felling till date by way of reducing the width of the road to 15 meters,” said UP’s PWD in an affidavit before NGT. Advertisement NGT is examining the issue of felling of more than 1 lakh trees and shrubs in the protected forest area of three forest divisions– Ghaziabad, Meerut and Muzaffarnagar for construction of two lanes of 111 km “Kawar Marg” from Muradnagar to Purkaji near Uttarakhand border.

title: Maharashtra postpones NDVI implementation to assess crop loss amid cabinet disagreements
Text: Maharashtra government has postponed the decision to use Normalised Difference vegetation index (NDVI) to assess crop loss due to drought and excessive rains till January 2025 owing to disagreement within the Cabinet. In a Cabinet meeting held on Tuesday Deputy Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis reportedly pushed the use of modern satellite technology and use of NDVI to access the damage to crops. Advertisement Despite his push, the Agriculture department has conveyed that implementation of NDVI will not be possible. “Ultimately, it was agreed to implement the system from January 2025,” an official who attended the meeting told The Indian Express. On February 5, 2024, Maharashtra cabinet had decided to use NDVI as the criteria to access crop losses.

title: ‘People have become more sensitive about their religions,’ HC quashes FIR against two accused of ‘outraging religious sentiments’
Text: The Nagpur bench of the Bombay High Court on Wednesday quashed a 2017 FIR filed against two persons, including an Army technician and a medical practitioner, who were accused of outraging the religious sentiments of Muslims through a WhatsApp group by asking certain members to “either say Vande Mataram or go to Pakistan.” The bench observed that “nowadays, people have become more sensitive about their religions, perhaps more than before, and everyone wants to emphasize how their religion or God is supreme.” Advertisement “We live in a democratic secular country where everyone should respect the religion, caste, creed, etc of others. However, we also believe that if someone claims their religion is supreme, others should not react impulsively.

title: VVIP security: Govt alerts DGs, cites attempt on Trump’s life
Text: Citing the recent assassination attempt on former US President Donald Trump, the central government has asked Director Generals of states, union territories and paramilitary forces to increase security measures so “high-risk dignitaries” can be kept safe, particularly during rallies, corner meetings, and roadshows. Trump survived an assassination attempt on July 13, while addressing a campaign rally near Pennsylvania. He was shot and wounded in his right ear by a 20-year-old man, who fired eight rounds with an AR-15–style rifle from the roof of a building. Advertisement The incident is one of seven assassination attempts cited by the Centre in its communication shared on July 16 with the DGs, including those in-charge of the CRPF, CISF, ITBP, NSG as well as state intelligence bureaus.

title: Railway Ministry allocated Rs 1,112.57 cr for Kavach in FY25, says Vaishnaw
Text: A sum of Rs 1,112.57 crore has been allocated for the installation of the Automatic Train Protection (ATP) system Kavach in the financial year of 2024-25, Railways Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said in a written reply in the Lok Sabha on Wednesday. Responding to the questions raised by DMK MPs Kanimozhi Karunanidhi and Rani Srikumar on the details regarding the funds allocated and utilised for installation of Kavach system in the country, Vaishnaw said: “The funds utilised on Kavach works so far is Rs1,216.77 crore. The allocation of funds during the year 2024-25 is Rs1,112.57 crore.” Kavach is an indigenous automatic train protection system. “Kavach aids the loco pilot in running the train within specified speed limits by automatic application of brakes,” Vaishnaw said.

title: Opp claims Budget discrimination, BJP says Govt has all states in mind
Text: THE OPPOSITION said in Lok Sabha Wednesday that the Union Budget was designed to save the coalition government at the Centre, alluding to the budgetary provisions for Andhra Pradesh and Bihar which are ruled by BJP allies TDP and JD(U), respectively. The Congress said it appears like the BJP has given up on the upcoming elections in Maharashtra, Haryana and J&K as there is not much for them in the Budget. The BJP hit back saying that while Andhra Pradesh and Bihar may not figure in the “Congress account”, the government has all states in mind. The TDP and JD(U) thanked the Centre for the allocations to their states. Advertisement Initiating the discussion on the Budget, Congress MP Selja Kumari said that she is thankful to the Finance Minister for “showing a big heart and reading the Congress manifesto” — a reiteration of the party’s claim that the government has borrowed its ideas. “We prepared it with a lot of hard work… They kept their guarantees on the side and used our manifesto. What do I say to this Budget? Whether to call it Kursi Bachao Budget or shaken-up Budget or Jumla Budget? We see jumlas in this,” she said.

title: Budget and BJP: Where govt kept the party’s manifesto promises – and where it didn’t
Text: WHILE THE Congress claimed that the third Narendra Modi government liberally borrowed from its Lok Sabha poll manifesto for its first Budget, Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman also set the ball rolling on some of the BJP’s promises while skipping others. The Budget, most prominently, skipped the BJP’s ambitious promise to bring all senior citizens above the age of 70 under its Ayushman Bharat cover, though it technically has four more years to follow through on its word. On MSMEs, agriculture, heritage, the BJP government followed through on what it had promised. Benefit for senior citizens: One major promise that was skipped was the extension of free healthcare under the Ayushman Bharat Yojana to all senior citizens above the age of 70. “We will expand the Ayushman Bharat Yojana to cover senior citizens and provide them access to free and quality healthcare,” the BJP manifesto said. Prime Minister Modi also mentioned this in many of his poll speeches. The Budget, however, made no mention of this. Incidentally, the health sector saw only a minor increase in allocation in the Budget, of 1.7%, to Rs 86,656 crore. The Ayushman Bharat health insurance scheme, which currently provides Rs 5 lakh cover to

title: Mumbai: After Tulsi, Tansa lake overflows; lake levels near 60 per cent
Text: Tansa, one of the seven lakes that cater to Mumbai’s water demands, started overflowing on Wednesday evening. In a relief to the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), the overall stock in the seven lakes also soared to 58.13 per cent (8.41 lakh million litres) of the total holding capacity, on Wednesday morning. Earlier this week, Tulsi, which is the smallest of the seven lakes, had also started overflowing on the morning of July 20. Situated in Thane district, the Tansa lake started overflowing at 4.19 pm on Wednesday, following which the BMC opened the three gates of the dam, resulting in the release of 3,315 cusecs of water.

title: Emissions by heavy vehicles on Mumbai-Pune expressway suggest need for stringent policies to curb vehicular pollution
Text: Amid rising concerns over air pollution and the major contribution of emissions from motor vehicles in urban parts of the country, a study of heavy polluter vehicles on the Mumbai-Pune expressway by researchers from the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Bombay suggests the need for stringent policies to restrict vehicular pollution. To conduct the study, the researchers set up their pollutant-measuring equipment at the entry and exit of the Kamshet-I tunnel located on the Mumbai-Pune expressway. According to researchers, roadway tunnels offer ideal conditions for this study because of the confined space within the tunnel, which effectively traps the emissions from the vehicles, barring the influence of other ambient sources.

title: Agniveer among three held for car snatching
Text: The district police on Wednesday arrested three individuals, including an Agniveer, for snatching a car at gunpoint. A .315 bore pistol with a live cartridge was also recovered. The arrested individuals were identified as Ishmeet Singh alias Ishu, Prabhpreet Singh alias Prabh, and Balkaran Singh, all residents of Fazilka. Mohali Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Dr Sandeep Garg stated that Ishmeet Singh, recruited as an Agniveer in 2022, was posted in West Bengal. He came on a one-month leave but did not return to duty. Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. “Ishmeet did not return to duty and started living in Balongi on rent with his brother Prabhpreet Singh and friend Balkaran Singh, engaging in thefts and snatchings,” SSP Garg said.

title: Himachal HC issues notice to Kangana, asks her to reply by Aug 21
Text: The Himachal Pradesh High Court on Wednesday issued a notice regarding a petition challenging the election of BJP MP Kangana Ranaut from the Mandi Lok Sabha seat. The court has ordered Ranaut to respond to the petition by August 21. The court of Justice Jyotsna Rewal Dua issued the notice on the petition of Kinnaur resident Layak Ram Negi, who had filled his nomination papers as an independent candidate for the Mandi seat but his nomination was rejected. In his petition, Negi requested to nullify the Lok Sabha election for the Mandi seat, alleging that his nomination papers were improperly rejected.

title: Mumbai: 52-year-old man stabbed to death inside spa in Worli
Text: A 52-year-old man was allegedly killed by two unknown persons inside a spa at Worli on Wednesday. The police said the deceased, who has worked as an RTI activist and also a police informer, had celebrated his birthday with the spa’s staffers before he was stabbed to death. According to the police, the incident took place at around 3 am on Wednesday. The deceased, identified as Guru Waghmare, a resident of Vile Parle, was a frequent visitor at Soft Touch Spa at Worli Naka. An officer said, “Waghmare’s birthday was on July 17 and as the staff of the spa were asking him for a party, he had taken four of them to a restaurant in Sion on Tuesday night. They all consumed alcohol there. One of the staff members is a 21-year-old woman.”

title: $1 trillion economy goal push: To push manufacturing, UP to develop 4 special investment regions in Aligarh, Unnao, Jhansi & Prayagraj
Text: With a focus on cluster-based development to achieve its 1-trillion dollar economy goal, the BJP government in Uttar Pradesh has identified Aligarh, Unnao, Jhansi and Prayagraj districts from the four geographical areas of the state to develop special investment regions (SIRs) for manufacturing by putting to use large chunks of “wasteland” available there, it is learnt. The Yogi Adityanath-led Cabinet had recently given the go-ahead to develop four SIRs in the state. While the Uttar Pradesh Nodal Investment Region for Manufacturing (NIRMAN) Bill will be tabled in the Assembly’s upcoming monsoon session starting July 29, the government has identified wasteland in Aligarh (west), Unnao (central), Prayagraj (east), and Jhansi (Bundelkhand) for the purpose. These districts not only have large chunks of wasteland but are also near the existing or the proposed expressways, officials said. While Aligarh is near the Yamuna Expressway, Unnao is alongside Lucknow-Agra Expressway. Advertisement For Jhansi, the state government has made budgetary provision to link it with the Bundelkhand Expressway through the Jhansi Link Expressway, while work is going on to connect Prayagraj with under-construction Ganga Expressway by the end of the year. “The idea is to have the special investment regions in four geographical regions of

title: At meet, farmer delegation reminds Rahul of MSP promise, he says will pressure govt
Text: The INDIA bloc will put pressure on the government and will explore all possibilities, including moving a Private Member’s Bill, to ensure farmers get a legal guarantee for MSP, Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi told a 12-member delegation of farm union leaders during a meeting in Parliament House on Wednesday. In the nearly 45-minute meeting, the delegation of farmer leaders from Punjab, Haryana, UP, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka apprised Gandhi of their issues, specifically the long-pending demand of a legal guarantee of minimum support price (MSP) for their crops. Gandhi assured the farm leaders — representatives of Sayunkt Kisan Morcha (non-political) and Kisan Mazdoor Morcha — that the legal guarantee for the MSP was their right and the INDIA bloc will ensure they get it.

title: Tripura Police issue warning against ethnic rumour-mongering on social media, say strict action will be taken against offenders
Text: The Tripura Police on Wednesday issued a terse warning against rumour-mongering after rumours spread that some miscreants asked tribals to leave big towns of the state. The police said those spreading misinformation will be dealt with strongly. The issue surfaced on social media just days after tension subsided at Gandatwisa in Tripura’s Dhalai district, where around 40 houses, 30 shops and a few vehicles were damaged on July 12. The violence had broken out following tension over the death of tribal youth Parameshwar Reang, who was earlier injured in a clash with local youths on July 7. title: Illegal forex trading case: ED searches at 4 cities, assets worth Rs 80 cr frozen
Text: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) Mumbai has conducted searches on July 22 at various locations in Mumbai, Kolkata, Delhi and Gurgaon as part of an ongoing investigation in the case related to illegal online forex trading through international brokers, namely the OctaFx trading app and octafx.com. During searches, movable properties in the form of bank funds, Demat account holdings to the tune of approximately Rs 80.43 crore have been frozen and various incriminating documents, digital devices have been recovered and seized, the central agency said on Wednesday. The total attachment and freezing in the case till date is approximately Rs 118 crore. Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. title: Seeping rainwater, dilapidated condition make quarters of medical staff at Sewri TB hospital unlivable
Text: Amid the ongoing monsoon rains, medical staff at Sewri TB Hospital—the largest TB hospital in the country—have been enduring a severe lack of electricity and water for nearly 36 hours. Rainwater is seeping through the walls of the quarters where medical staff, including doctors, reside, adding to their woes. Doctors at Sewri TB Hospital are housed in three adjacent buildings, each over 50 years old and four stories high. These quarters are in precarious condition, putting the lives of nearly 40 to 50 medical officers and their families at risk, according to residents. Nearly 15 doctors and their families live in the A and B wings, which are in urgent need of repairs as plaster falls from ceilings and water leaks through walls during the monsoon. title: NASA telescope spots a super Jupiter that takes over a century to go around its star
Text: A super Jupiter has been spotted around a neighboring star by the Webb Space Telescope — and it has a super orbit. The planet is roughly the same diameter as Jupiter, but with six times the mass. Its atmosphere is also rich in hydrogen like Jupiter’s. One big difference: It takes this planet more than a century, possibly as long as 250 years, to go around its star. It’s 15 times the distance from its star than Earth is to the sun. Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. title: Could Moon have a cave system? NASA finds out
Text: A team of scientists discovered evidence of caves on the Moon’s surface using data from NASA’s LRO (Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter). Data collected by LRO’s Mini-RF (Miniature Radio-Frequency) instrument in 2010 found evidence that a cave extends over 200 feet from the base of a pit, which is located 230 miles northeast where the Apollo 11 mission landed on July 20, 1969. The full extent of the cave, located near the Sea of Tranquility, is unknown but is expected to stretch for miles, according to NASA. Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. Like ‘lava tubes’ on Earth, scientists suspect that the lunar caves were formed when molten lava flowed beneath a field of cooled lava, or a crust formed over a river of lava, leaving a long, hollow tunnel. If the ceiling of a solidified lava tube collapses, it opens a pit, like a skylight, that can lead into the rest of the cave-like tube.

title: 38-year-old engineer jumps off Atal Setu, search on to locate him
Text: A 38-year-old engineer allegedly jumped off the Atal Setu on Wednesday. The police, Coast Guard and local fishermen are trying to locate him. The police said the engineer, Karuturi Srinivas, was deep in debt. According to the police, Srinivas lived in Palava city, Dombivali. “He was married and earlier worked in Kuwait. In 2023, he came back to India and started his own company along with a partner, which dealt in electrical contracts in residential buildings,” a police officer said. The police said Srinivas went to the bridge in his Tata Nexon car, stopped his vehicle on the bridge and then jumped off. “After we learnt about the incident, we located his car from CCTV footage. We found his Aadhaar card in his car,” the officer said.

After collecting evidence against them, a chargesheet has been filed with the honourable court against them,” Gohil said. “The chargesheet runs into more than one lakh pages,” he added.

title: Deshmukh alleges Fadnavis pressured him to implicate Thackerays
Text: Former Maharashtra Home Minister Anil Deshmukh on Wednesday alleged that an intermediary of BJP leader and Deputy CM Devendra Fadnavis had asked him to provide affidavits against important figures in the Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA) government to avoid getting embroiled in litigation himself, an allegation Fadnavis has denied. Deshmukh has alleged that he was instructed by the intermediary to accuse Uddhav Thackeray of soliciting funds for the municipal elections and was also asked to accuse Aaditya Thackeray of involvement in the death of Disha Salian. “I refused to make that accusation,” he stated, speaking from Nagpur. I will reveal it at the appropriate time,” he said.

title: Dead woman, two children thrown in river: Cops probe sequence of events at Kalamboli hospital
Text: THE Pimpri Chinchwad police have started probing the sequence of events that took place at a hospital at Kalamboli in Navi Mumbai as part of their investigation into the death of a 25-year-old pregnant woman, whose dead body was thrown into Indrayani river on the Talegaon Chakan road in Pune, along with her two sons when they were still alive. A team from the Pimpri Chinchwad police station visited the hospital on Wednesday and were in the process of questioning doctors, staff and others connected to the incident, said a police officer. The investigation by Pimpri Chinchwad police into the missing persons case of the pregnant woman from Talegaon Dabhade and her children revealed on Sunday that the body of the woman, who had died at a hospital in Kalamboli on July 8, was thrown into Indrayani river on the Talegaon Chakan road in Pune on July 9, along with her two sons. The woman had been taken to the hospital to perform a Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP).

title: An outlining of urban transformation strategies
Text: Cities are home to about 50 crore people, accounting for about 36% of India’s population. The urban population has been growing at a steady pace of 2% to 2.5% annually. The ever-growing pace of urbanisation in India calls for sustained investments, with a vision and determination. The maiden Budget of the new government has recognised cities as the growth hubs and offered many options and opportunities for the planned development and the growth of cities. The Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban) has been under implementation since 2015 and has provided as many as 85 lakh housing units for the Economically Weaker Sections (EWS)-Middle Income Groups (MIG) categories of population, with an investment of about ₹8 lakh crore. Of this, a quarter has been provided by the central government and the remaining by the beneficiaries and State governments. title: Top 500 companies will not be forced for internship programme, say govt sources
Text: Government sources have said that the top 500 companies will not be forced for the internship programme announced in the Union Budget. As outlined by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in the Union Budget 2024, the government will provide a stipend for the internships. “No company will be forced into the internship programme as announced in the budget. The government will provide money for internships, while companies will bear the cost of training the interns through corporate social responsibility (CSR),” government sources told ANI on Wednesday. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced on Tuesday that the government will launch a scheme to offer internship opportunities to youth in the top 500 companies in India as part of the Union Budget 2024-25. The scheme, which will be implemented over the next five years, is expected to benefit 100 million youth. Interns will receive a monthly stipend of Rs 5,000 and a one-time assistance of Rs 6,000. Companies will cover training costs and 10 per cent of the internship costs from CSR funds. Text: Axis Bank, India’s fourth-largest private bank by market capitalisation, reported a smaller-than-expected first-quarter profit on Wednesday as higher provisions weighed and margins shrunk. The Mumbai-based lender’s standalone net profit – which excludes its subsidiaries – rose 4% year-on-year to 60.35 billion rupees ($721.2 million) for the quarter ended June 30. Analysts had estimated a profit of 64.50 billion rupees, as per LSEG data. Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. Provisions and contingencies, or funds kept aside for potential bad loans, rose 97% to 20.39 billion rupees. Lenders typically choose how much they want to set aside to cover potential bad loans and against any unforeseen events. Axis Bank’s gross non-performing assets ratio, a key gauge of lenders’ asset quality, rose to 1.54% at the end of June from 1.43% in the previous quarter, indicating deterioration.

title: Body of sailor who went missing after INS Brahmaputra fire recovered: Navy
Text: THREE DAYS after a fire broke out onboard Navy’s guided missile frigate INS Brahmaputra, divers early Wednesday recovered the body of a 25-year-old Leading Seaman, who had gone missing since the incident. Colaba police filed an accidental death report after the recovery of the body. The Leading Seaman was identified as Sitendra Puran Singh from Surajgarh, Rajasthan. Advertisement Navy officers said INS Brahmaputra was undergoing a refit at Mumbai Harbour when the fire broke out Sunday. It was noticed by the ship’s duty staff while carrying out routine maintenance work. Navy has ordered an inquiry. The Navy said in a statement that it stands resolutely with the bereaved family in this hour of grief.

title: Assam police search Cong MLA’s home in MP over cheating case against his son
Text: A police team from Assam on Wednesday searched the residence of a Congress MLA in Madhya Pradesh’s Tikamgarh city over a cheating case registered against his son, an official said. The team of cops reached the Congress MLA and former minister Yadvendra Singh Bundela’s home, located in the Tal Darwaja area of the city, he said. Superintendent of Police (SP) Rohit Kashwani said a case of cheating has been registered against the lawmaker’s son, Shashwat Singh , in Assam. Story continues below. Keshwani said the team returned after a search at the home of Bundela, who represents the Tikamgarh assembly constituency, for three hours under the protection of local police.

title: Minimum wage: As Congress calls for Rs 400 a day, what does govt say, where does MGNREGA stand
Text: Written by Sanjana Suchdev Highlighting “the decline in real wages”, the Congress demanded a nationwide minimum wage of Rs 400 per day ahead of the Union Budget. Congress general secretary, communications, Jairam Ramesh said multiple sources, including government data, indicate that “workers can buy less today than they could 10 years ago”. He cited the Labour Bureau’s Wage Rate Index while saying “real wages for labourers stagnated between 2014-2023, and in fact declined between 2019-2024.” Ramesh also referred to the Union Ministry of Agriculture’s data showing that under then Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, real wages for farm labourers grew at 6.8% annually, whereas under PM Narendra Modi, they declined by 1.3% each year. Adding that the Budget was an opportunity to correct this, Ramesh posted on X: “(It) offers (the PM) the chance to achieve what the Congress has called ‘Asli 400 paar’.” In line with Congress manifesto The Congress’s Lok Sabha election manifesto included promises focusing on workers, including a Right to Health law and an employment guarantee for urban areas, a review of labour codes under the Modi government, curbs on the contractualisation of labour, an increase in the national minimum wage to Rs 400 per day, and

title: Mamata Banerjee seeks stay on order restraining her from making any ‘defamatory’ comment against Governor
Text: West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee on Wednesday moved a Division Bench of the Calcutta High Court, seeking a stay on a single bench order that restrained her and three other TMC leaders from making “defamatory or incorrect statements” against Governor CV Ananda Bose. Challenging the single bench’s interim order, Banerjee and the three others — two newly-elected TMC MLAs Sayantika Banerjee and Reyat Hossain Sarkar, and TMC spokesperson Kunak Ghosh — filed an appeal before the Division Bench of Justice I P Mukerji and Justice Biswaroop Chowdhury. Advertisement Seeking a stay on the single bench order of Justice Krishna Rao, the chief minister’s counsel S N Mookherjee said that Banerjee did not make any defamatory statement against the Governor.

title: Four injured in fire at high-rise in Jogeshwari
Text: Four persons including two women were injured after a fire broke out at a high-rise in Jogeshwari on Wednesday morning. While no casualties were reported, the four were admitted to a hospital owing to suffocation. The incident took place at 8.58 am inside a Ground-plus-24 storey residential building, which also houses commercial establishments, situated along the SV Road in Jogeshwari West. According to senior officials from Mumbai Fire Brigade (MFB), the fire sparked in the electrical duct of the building and spread to the electric wiring and other installations through the duct between the fifteenth and the twentieth floors of the building.

title: Rain batters south, central Gujarat districts, hundreds relocated
Text: Hundreds of people were evacuated after swollen rivers and overflowing dams cut-off several villages and inundated low-lying areas in many parts of Gujarat amid torrential downpours on Wednesday. Normal life was thrown out of gear as heavy rain pounded south and central Gujarat districts like Surat, Bharuch and Anand since morning, prompting the authorities to declare a holiday for schools and colleges in some places. Train services were also affected in some areas. A red alert was issued for Vadodara city, with Vishwamitri river swelling up to 18.3 feet, posing a danger of a flood if it touched 22 feet. The administration in the rain-battered districts deployed personnel from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) and local fire teams to rescue people from flooded areas and relocate them to safe places. Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. Heavy rain that hit Surat on Tuesday flooded the city and cut-off several villages, necessitating relocation of around 200 people, officials said. As many as 132 roads in the district were blocked as a precautionary measure. title: Kolkata sees ‘37% drop in dengue cases, 67% drop in malaria’ compared to July last year
Text: With the onset of monsoon, the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) announced a significant decline in cases of malaria and dengue in the city compared to last year’s numbers. According to data from KMC officials, a reduction of 37% was recorded in the dengue cases recorded in the area this year, standing at nearly 140 cases compared to 220 cases recorded around January to July 14 last year. Advertisement As of July 14 this year, 2,100 dengue cases have been reported in the state. As for cases of malaria, 863 have been reported so far in comparison to more than 2002 cases this time last year, with a reduction of 67%.

title: Kannada TV serial actor Sunny Mahipal booked for assaulting pregnant ‘wife’ in Bengaluru
Text: A pregnant woman, who claimed to be the wife of Kannada television actor Sunny Mahipal, accused him of assaulting her with a knife in Bengaluru on Monday, leading the police to book a case against the actor on the same day. The incident reportedly took place at the actor’s house in Vignan Nagar near Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL). The woman sustained deep cut injuries on her left arm and the attack also led to a miscarriage, the police said. In her complaint, the woman said she is a law graduate and had met Mahipal through social media in February. The two soon got into a relationship.

title: ‘Stock market scam’: 2 senior citizens lose Rs 96 lakh in Maharashtra
Text: Two senior citizens, one from Thane and the other from Navi Mumbai, collectively lost Rs 96 lakh this week in what the Maharashtra Police are claiming to be a ‘stock market scam’. Stock market scams have become widespread in the past few months with several persons, especially senior citizens, losing money after getting lured by high returns. Some fraudsters have also started issuing online ads asking people to contact them if they want to invest money and the police are unable to put a stop to these scams. In the Thane case, a 65-year-old man, who recently retired as an administrator, wanted to invest his life savings in the share market. In May, when he was watching videos online, he saw an ‘IIFL’ advertisement. Assuming it to be the real investment company, he sent a text message to the number provided in the advertisement. The person then added him to a WhatsApp group.

title: In major bureaucratic reshuffle in Delhi, 8 IAS officers transferred and posted
Text: Lieutenant Governor V K Saxena on Wednesday affected the transfers of over half a dozen senior Indian Administrative Service (IAS) and DANICS officers across departments under the Delhi government as well as those beyond its jurisdiction. In the transfers and postings announced by the Delhi government’s services department, six of the IAS officers who were part of the overhaul were awaiting postings and belonged to the Arunachal Pradesh-Goa-Mizoram and Union Territory (AGMUT) or Central cadres and batches from 1996 to 2008. Advertisement A Anbarasu, a 1996-batch IAS officer of the AGMUT cadre — who held three significant charges including that of principal secretary, Public Works Department, Trade and Taxes as well CEO of the Delhi Jal Board — was relieved of the charge of Principal Secretary, Trade and Taxes.

title: ‘Case of trust deficit’: SC orders status quo at Shambhu border, proposes independent panel to talk to farmers
Text: Ordering a status quo at the Shambhu border where restrictions have been put in place by Haryana to regulate the crossing over of protesting farmers from Punjab, the Supreme Court on Wednesday said it proposed to form a committee of independent people to negotiate with the farmers and resolve the issues. “We are proposing to constitute some independent committee comprising of persons who can reach out to farmers and to suggest where they are wrong or right and can communicate with other stakeholders also,” a bench of Justices Surya Kant, Dipankar Datta and Ujjal Bhuyan said, and asked the two states to take instructions about this and suggest names of people who can be included in the proposed committee. Advertisement Justice Surya Kant said that “it is a case of trust deficit” and added, “We will think of some independent persons, who are neutral to the controversy”. “Till such times, both states are directed to maintain the status quo at the site…to prevent flaring up the situation at the Shambhu border,” the bench said. The court was hearing Haryana’s plea seeking a stay on the Punjab and Haryana High Court directive to open the border on an experimental basis. The

title: In Rajya Sabha, Opp corners govt on allocation to Andhra Pradesh, Bihar
Text: A day after Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman presented the first Budget of the new NDA government, Opposition parties in Rajya Sabha accused the Centre of splurging on the ally-ruled Andhra Pradesh and Bihar at the cost of other states. They also said the government had failed to address crucial issues such as inflation and unemployment. Leading the discussion was former finance minister and senior Congress leader P Chidambaram, who said the government had “copied” parts of his party’s poll manifesto. Advertisement “I am particularly happy that she (Sitharaman) had an opportunity to read the Congress manifesto. I would urge friends on treasury benches to read the Congress manifesto so that in your party meetings, you can persuade the prime minister and the finance minister to take some more ideas from our manifesto,” he said. “Copying is not prohibited in this house, in fact, copying is encouraged, rewarded in this house. Please copy a little more.” Chidambaram expressed scepticism about the production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme’s impact on job creation, suggesting that the shift to employment-linked incentive might be an admission of PLI’s shortcomings.

title: Kharge recalls ‘groundbreaking’ 1991 budget, says there’s pressing need for meaningful reforms
Text: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Wednesday said his party takes immense pride in the groundbreaking achievement of the Liberalisation Budget of 1991, and asserted that there is a pressing need once again for meaningful and robust second-generation reforms. In a post on X, Kharge said July 1991 marked a watershed moment in India’s history as the Liberalisation Budget, spearheaded by then Prime Minister P V Narasimha Rao and Finance Minister Manmohan Singh, ushered in a new era of economic reforms. This visionary move revolutionised the country, empowering the middle class and uplifting millions from poverty and marginalisation, he said. Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. “The Congress party takes immense pride in this groundbreaking achievement, which catalysed India’s growth trajectory and continues to inspire progress and prosperity,” Kharge said.

Text: It was a day of wait and meetings with Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini, apart from sports officials, for Tokyo Paralympics multiple medallist and shooter Singhraj Adhana and parents of Paris Olympics qualified Haryana players and Asian Para Games/Asian Games, CWG medallists for the delay in getting cash awards for national and international events, including Para Asian games and ISSF World Cup/Championships. title: As Apple Watch’s ‘Family Setup’ arrives in India, Cupertino introduces a new way for parents and kids to communicate
Text: Apple introduced a new feature for the Apple Watch in India on Wednesday, allowing parents to enable children to make and receive phone calls, FaceTime audio calls, and text messages directly from their wrist without needing an iPhone. This feature, known as “Family Setup,” was rolled out during the pandemic with watchOS 7 but was unavailable in India at that time. Now, Apple is launching it in India. For years, the Apple Watch has been primarily seen as an iPhone accessory. However, with the introduction of the Apple Watch’s new Family Setup function, designed for kids and the elderly, they can now make phone calls, exchange text messages, and share their GPS location with family members independently of an iPhone. Until recently, setting up an Apple Watch required an iPhone, which was convenient for existing iPhone users. However, it was not possible to use the Apple Watch as a standalone device for a child or elderly person at home. title: Rupee hits record low amid pressure on local equities
Text: e Indian rupee weakened to its lowest level on record on Wednesday, pressured by the decline in local equities after the government’s decision to raise the tax rate on capital gains dampened market sentiment. The rupee declined to 83.72 to the dollar, slipping below the previous all-time low of 83.7150 hit on Tuesday. Benchmark Indian equity indices, the BSE Sensex and Nifty 50, were down about 0.3% and 0.2% each on Wednesday. The Reserve Bank of India had likely intervened to support the rupee earlier in the session, traders said.

title: Cow smuggler shot dead while being chased by police in Rajasthan
Text: A pickup van driver allegedly smuggling cows was shot dead in the early hours of Wednesday by another group of suspected bovine smugglers in Rajasthan’s Deeg district, police said. Superintendent of Police (SP) Rajesh Kumar Meena said the incident occurred around 2 am, adding that police had information that two men were smuggling cows in a pickup van. As a police team gave the vehicle a chase, the occupants of the pickup truck opened fire at it, he said. Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. Meena said that at some distance, two other suspected cow smugglers were catching bovines. Seeing the commotion, they opened fire at the pickup van, the officer added.

title: ‘At least we believe in judicial propriety’: SC bench objects to another bench also initiating contempt proceedings in DDA case
Text: A Supreme Court Court Bench led by Justice B R Gavai on Wednesday said another Bench led by Justice A S Oka had “not adhered to judicial propriety” by acting on a contempt plea against the Delhi Development Authority (DDA) in the tree-felling case, pointing out that it had already issued notice in the matter. “The Additional Solicitor General (ASG) had informed the other Bench that this court is already seized of the matter, that this court has already issued notice for contempt,” Justice Gavai said. The Bench, also comprising Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and K V Viswanathan, referred the matter to Chief Justice of India D Y Chandrachud, asking him to decide which Bench should continue to hear the case so as to avoid conflicting orders. “Though the other Bench has not adhered to judicial propriety, we are doing so… When, for the same cause of action for felling of trees, this court had issued notice, could the other Bench have proceeded for that,” Justice Gavai asked. title: From the Urdu Press: ‘SC order on Kanwar Yatra row inspires hope’, ‘Akhilesh in wings aggravating BJP problems in UP’
Text: The first Budget of the Narendra Modi government after returning to power for the third consecutive term reflected the changed political landscape shaped by the outcome of the Lok Sabha polls. Unlike PM Modi’s first two terms, the BJP now relies on its allies TDP and JD(U) to remain in power, which defined the Union Budget for 2024-25 substantially. Shining light on this new reality, the Urdu dailies also flagged concerns that the Budget left a large section of the deprived as well as farmers in the cold. Hailing the Supreme Court’s order staying the directives issued by the police in BJP-ruled Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand asking food outlets, dhabas, and carts on the Kanwar Yatra route to display the names of their owners and employees, the multi-edition Roznama Rashtriya Sahara, in its editorial on July 23, says these directives were ostensibly meant to ascertain the religious identity of these eateries’ owners and staff. “These directives were arbitrary and cynical, which were aimed at driving a wedge between communities on the basis of religion,” it says. title: Nandi Hills ropeway project: Karnataka Govt tables Bill for land transfer
Text: The much-hyped ropeway project at Nandi Hills, a prime tourist spot near Bengaluru, appears to be inching closer to completion after the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) (Amendment) Bill 2024 was tabled in the Assembly on Wednesday to ease its implementation. According to the Bill, two acres of land at Nandi Hills will be provided for the construction of the upper terminal point of the 2.93-km-long ropeway. The land will be leased for 30 years for the project coming up under the public-private partnership model. Amendments are being introduced to section 5 of The Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Act 1975. The section provides for cases where the Government can alienate an area belonging to gardens run by the horticultural department for other activities. Though the foundation stone was laid in March 2023, the project has progressed at a snail’s pace owing to issues related to land transfers from various departments.

title: Either jail or ‘jahannum’ for terrorists: Union minister Rai on J&K terror attacks
Text: Terrorists active in Jammu and Kashmir will either land in jail or be sent to ‘jahannum’ (hell), Minister of State for Home Affairs Nityanand Rai said in the Rajya Sabha on Wednesday while asserting that the Modi government has zero tolerance for terrorism. Rai was replying to a supplementary question from Congress MP Pramod Tiwari. Terrorist activities witnessed recently will soon end, the minister said. “They (terrorists) will not succeed in their design,” he added. Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. In the past few days, 28 terrorists have been killed in Jammu and Kashmir and some security personnel have also lost their lives, which is very unfortunate, Rai said.

title: Jharkhand: 27 ‘stranded’ labourers return to Ranchi from Cameroon
Text: A total of 27 labourers from Jharkhand, who were reportedly stranded in Central Africa’s Cameroon, returned to the state on Wednesday, officials said. The labourers had sought help from the state government, through a recent video message, claiming they were not receiving their salaries from the employer and also facing trouble in arranging for daily meals. Subsequently, Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren wrote a letter to the Ministry of External Affairs, urging the safe return of the migrant workers, according to an official release. Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads. “We received information about the problems of 27 people of Jharkhand stranded in Cameroon, Africa. Thereafter, the Jharkhand government took the initiative and got the outstanding amount of about Rs 30 lakh paid to them, and brought them back to the state,” Soren said on X.

title: Centre, Opposition face off in Parliament over Budget
Text: In both Houses of Parliament, the Opposition attacked the government, accusing it of presenting a “discriminatory budget” that excluded the non-National Democratic Alliance (NDA)-ruled States. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman issued a strong rebuttal to this in Rajya Sabha, hitting out at the Opposition for deliberately maligning the government, and giving a wrong impression that some States had been left out. The Rajya Sabha saw a sharp exchange of words between the two sides on Wednesday morning. The Opposition staged a walkout in protest. Congress president and Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge said that only two States had benefited from the Union Budget, presented on Tuesday. He said it was a budget aimed solely at safeguarding the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led NDA government. “I condemn all this. Opposition party-ruled States have been neglected. How will development happen if there is no balance? I condemn this and all the parties condemn this type of attitude,” Mr. Kharge said. Ms. Sitharaman reacted strongly to the accusation, saying that all the States could not be named in the budget, and the Congress, which had been in power for long, should know better than to make such an allegation. title: Triple-balance sheet Union Budget
Text: The Union Budget presented yesterday uses the formidable Triple Balance Sheet advantage that India has meticulously developed. While operational details of the budget have been widely discussed, the central theme of this budget demands attention. It is misleading to label this as a political budget due to the nature of the coalition government. Instead, it strategically supports various states and social development projects without draining the Government of India coffers. This budget exemplifies fiscal discipline without yielding to the temptation of pleasing every constituency, yet maintains sufficient optics to satisfy most stakeholders. Like a household budget or corporate business plan, it is impossible to please everyone. With tax revenues showing remarkable buoyancy, projections for the upcoming financial year indicate higher revenues than those in the Interim Budget. Considering this revenue buoyancy and the RBI dividend, the government can effectively balance cutting the fiscal deficit slightly, increasing capex, and boosting social welfare projects. This is precisely what the Union Budget FY25 has outlined. By leveraging the Triple Balance Sheet advantage, the budget ensures fiscal prudence while fostering growth, social welfare, and economic stability. title: Panchamasali Lingayat council asks Karnataka govt to clarify legal stand on OBC quota demand
Text: A group of advocates from the Lingayat subsect of Panchamasalis met on Tuesday to discuss and plan a legal strategy for resuming their agitation to seek reservations for the community under the OBC 2A category. They have requested clarification from the Karnataka Congress government regarding the state’s legal stance on the community’s demand for Other Backward Classes (OBC) quota. The Congress government has been called upon to clarify its position within a month on the Panchamasali community’s demand for inclusion in the OBC 2A category. This inclusion would allow the community to benefit from a 15 per cent quota in government jobs and educational opportunities for OBC communities. This resolution was one of four passed by the Panchamasali lawyers council on Tuesday. “The government should immediately call a meeting of its legal department and clarify within a month about the Panchamasali 2A and Lingayat OBC reservations,” said a resolution passed by the Panchamasali advocates council in the presence of the Lingayat seer Basavaraj Mruthyunjaya Swamy. title: Rain slows down in city, weekend may see moderate showers
Text: After a week of receiving nearly 100 mm rain daily, the severity of showers took a beating with gusty winds and light showers sweeping Mumbai even as the India Meteorological Department (IMD) upgraded to an orange alert in the district on Wednesday afternoon. According to the weather bureau, the intensity is slated to reduce in the coming days with the IMD issuing a yellow alert in the city between Thursday and Friday. The city is likely to get moderate rains during the weekend. Amid ongoing rains, the city has already clocked in nearly 80 percent of its annual average quota of rainfall. Data showed that between Tuesday and Wednesday morning, the city sought respite in moderate showers with IMD’s Santacruz station recording 46 mm rain while the Colaba observatory registered 38 mm rain.

title: TMC moves resolution against NEET in West Bengal assembly
Text: The Trinamool Congress Wednesday moved a resolution in the Assembly condemning the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET), and demanding that the Joint Entrance Examination (JEE) be reinstated in West Bengal. A motion moved by the TMC and passed through voice vote said, “This House, while strongly condemning the failure of National Testing Agency (NTA) to conduct undergraduate and postgraduate examinations fairly and freely, urges the Government of West Bengal to conduct the JEE for ensuring a robust public healthcare system across the state, particularly in far-fledged rural areas, in public interest.” The resolution, moved by TMC MLAs Sobhandeb Chattopadhyay, Firhad Hakim, Aroop Biswas, Shashi Panja, Chandrima Bhattacharya, Nirmal Ghosh and Ashok Kumar Deb, stated, “Previously for the state quota of undergraduate and postgraduate seats in medical colleges in West Bengal, JEE was conducted by the Joint Entrance Board, which has since been abolished due to the NEET coming into force.”

title: Hours before its release, Kerala HC stays Hema Commission report that exposes problems faced by women in Malayalam film industry
Text: Hours before its findings were to be made public, the Kerala High Court Wednesday stayed the release of a report on the problems faced by women in the Malayalam movie industry. The report had been prepared by the state government-appointed Justice K Hema Commission. Advertisement The court’s interim stay on the findings of the commission came on the back of a petition by filmmaker Saji Parayil, who challenged the state information commission’s July 6 directive ordering that the findings be made public. The panel was set up in 2017 after a prominent woman actor was abducted and sexually assaulted in a moving car near Kochi.

title: Watch: YS Sharmila walks into floodwaters, slams BJP’s ‘partisan attitude’ towards Andhra Pradesh
Text: In an effort to draw the central government’s attention to the flood-hit regions in Andhra Pradesh, state Congress President YS Sharmila walked waist-deep into floodwaters on Wednesday, criticising the BJP government’s ‘partisan attitude’ towards the state. Text: TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee Wednesday targeted the ruling NDA over the Union Budget 2024 and highlighted the failures of the government raising temperatures in the Parliament. Participating in the discussion on Budget 2024-25, he said the budget presented by Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman is “anti-people” and aimed at “appeasing and compensating” coalition partners of the ruling NDA. “Coalition means cooperation, collaboration, cohesion. But after yesterday, coalition is appeasement and compensation,” said Banerjee, adding that in 2024 people rejected the Modi-led BJP government and the country has a shaky coalition now which is so uncertain and fragile that it can implode anytime. “BJP is ensnared in tentacles of appeasement politics trying to save its own chair,” said Banerjee. “Message is loud and clear — waqt badal gaya hain. title: ‘TMC MLA tried to assault me on Assembly premises’: West Bengal BJP Opposition leader
Text: Leader of Opposition of West Bengal Assembly Suvendu Adhikari alleged Wednesday that a TMC MLA tried to assault him and he requested the Speaker to take action. Speaker Biman Banerjee said he has ordered an investigation. According to sources, after a question-answer session at the Assembly lobby, there was an altercation between the Leader of Opposition and the MLA of Purbasthali, Tapan Chatterjee. During the session, BJP MLA Shankar Ghosh reportedly mentioned this to the Speaker, who said to “not discuss the matter here” and In his letter, Adhikari wrote, “… Today at around 12.20 pm at the lower lobby …Chatterjee …rushed towards me and tried to assault me physically and threw abusive language in front of other MLAs and reporters. title: 10 years after landslide, 7 years since rehabilitation: Survivors and crippled gram panchayat await land transfer in Malin
Text: It’s been 10 years since the Malin tragedy of July 30, 2014, that claimed lives of 151 villagers and seven years since the state government handed over the keys of homes to the survivors in the ‘New Malin’–about a kilometre away from the site of one of the biggest landslide incidents in the world. The rehabilitated village with 68 ‘landslide, earthquake resistant homes’, a school, temple, gram panchayat office and other community spaces was developed by the state government at a cost of Rs 27 crore and handed over to the survivors of the tragedy on April 2, 2017. However, on record, the land still remains with the revenue department with the transfer of ownership stuck in the administrative red-tape. title: 3 die of Japanese encephalitis in Assam’s Morigaon
Text: Three persons from Assam’s Morigaon district have died due to Japanese encephalitis, an official said on Wednesday. At present, 11 patients are undergoing treatment for the disease, and their conditions are stated to be stable, he said. Among the deceased was Rajamani Medhi, 22, who died at the Gauhati Medical College and Hospital on Wednesday, after being diagnosed with the disease last week, he added. Story continues below. title: Under NEET-UG heat, Bihar replicates anti-cheating law of Centre, other states
Text: Bihar on Wednesday joined the list of states to have passed an anti-cheating law, with its Assembly clearing the Bihar Public Examinations (PE) (Prevention of Unfair Means) Bill, 2024, amid a walkout by the Opposition. This comes amidst the conclusion by a probe into the NEET-UG exam irregularities, which have rocked Parliament, that the cheating incident happened in Bihar. The new legislation aims at curbing malpractices in competitive examinations, including the leak of question papers, and stipulates severe punishment for those involved in such malpractices, including a prison term of three to five years, and a fine of Rs 10 lakh. In February, the Centre passed The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Bill, 2024, proposing a minimum three to five years of imprisonment for accused. title: CERT-In reported possible intrusion, data breach at BSNL on May 20: MoS Communications
Text: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) had reported possible intrusion and data breach at state-owned Bharat Sanchar Nigam Ltd (BSNL) on May 20, 2024, Parliament was informed on Wednesday. An Inter Ministerial Committee (IMC) has been constituted to conduct an audit of the telecom networks and suggest remedial measures for prevention of data breaches in the telecom networks, Minister of State for Communications Pemmasani Chandra Sekhar said in a written reply in the Lok Sabha. To a question on data breach in BSNL, the Minister informed that Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) reported possible intrusion and data breach at BSNL on May 20, 2024.

title: MP: Labourer digs a fortune, uncovers diamond worth Rs 80 lakh from Panna mine
Text: A labourer found a 19.22-carat diamond in a mine in Madhya Pradesh’s Panna district on Wednesday which could fetch about Rs 80 lakh or more at the government auction, officials said. Raju Gaud said when he set out in the morning to dig mud and sift through it, a daily routine in monsoon months for the past ten years, he hadn’t imagined he would strike a fortune. “I hope the amount earned (after the auction) will reduce my financial hardships and take care of my children’s education,” Gaud said. The labourer said he was exulted after finding the precious stone in a leased mine at Krishna Kalyanpur and promptly deposited it with the government authorities.

Text: Synopsis Industry leaders and economists gathered in Kolkata to discuss the Union Budget 2024-25. Sandeep Kumar from CII West Bengal highlighted the 17% increase in capital expenditure and the focus on youth skilling initiatives. Debasish Dutta appreciated the formation of trade clusters and emphasized the need to boost inland water transport. Subir Chakraborty, former President of The Bengal Chamber, commended the budget's support for MSMEs and the government's effort to skill the workforce. title: Naxalite surrenders in Maharashtra’s Gadchiroli
Text: A Naxalite carrying a reward of Rs 2 lakh on his head on Wednesday surrendered before security forces in Maharashtra’s Gadchiroli district, officials said. Lachhu Kariya Tado (45), a member of the Bhamragad LOS (Local Organisation Squad) of the Naxalites, surrendered before police and Central Reserve Police Force officials.
